title.zh: 卷一百四十八 列傳第九十八: 裴垍 李吉甫 李籓 權德輿
title.en: Volume 148 Biographies 98: Pei Ji, Li Jifu, Li Fan, Quan Deyu
title.raw: 卷一百四十八 列傳第九十八: 裴垍 李吉甫 李籓 權德輿 Volume 148 Biographies 98: Pei Ji, Li Jifu, Li Fan, Quan Deyu

sentences.zh: 裴垍字弘中，河東聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Ji, style Hongzhong, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji, whose style was Hongzhong, came from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中宰相居道七代孫。

translations.literal: He was a seventh-generation descendant of the Chancellor Judao of the Zhonggong era.
translations.idiomatic: He was seven generations removed from Chancellor Pei Judao of the Zhonggong reign.

sentences.zh: 垍弱冠舉進士。

translations.literal: At his coming of age Ji passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he passed the jinshi civil examination.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，制舉賢良極諫，對策第一，授美原縣尉。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era, in the decree examination for Worthy and Outspoken Remonstrators, his policy essay ranked first, and he was appointed magistrate of Meiyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyuan he took the special examination for worthy remonstrators, placed first in the policy response, and was made magistrate of Meiyuan County.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，籓府交辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: When his term expired, regional administrations repeatedly invited him, but he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, several provincial staffs sought him out in turn, yet he declined every offer.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史，轉殿中侍御史、尚書禮部考功二員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor, then transferred to attendant censor in the Palace Secretariat and concurrently served as two assistant directors in the Ministry of Rites and the Ministry of Personnel for examinations and merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an investigating censor, then promoted to palace attendant censor and concurrent assistant director in both the Rites and Personnel ministries for examinations and merit records.

sentences.zh: 時吏部侍郎鄭珣瑜請垍考詞判，垍守正不受請托，考核皆務才實。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister of Personnel Zheng Xunyu asked Ji to grade examination essays; Ji upheld integrity and accepted no solicitations, and in every assessment he sought only talent and substance.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister Zheng Xunyu of Personnel asked him to grade examination papers, Ji held the line and refused favors, judging every candidate on genuine ability.

sentences.zh: 元和初，召入翰林為學士，轉考功郎中、知制誥，尋遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as academician, transferred to director of examinations in the Ministry of Personnel and drafter of edicts, and soon promoted to Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he entered the Hanlin as an academician, became director of examinations with charge of edicts, and soon rose to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫自翰林承旨拜平章事，詔將下之夕，感出涕。

translations.literal: Li Jifu, from Hanlin chief academician, was appointed Grand Councilor; on the evening when the edict was about to be issued, moved, he shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jifu was promoted from chief Hanlin academician to Grand Councilor, he wept the night the edict was to be promulgated.

sentences.zh: 謂垍曰：「吉甫自尚書郎流落遠地，十余年方歸，便入禁署，今才滿歲，後進人物，罕所接識。

translations.literal: He said to Ji: "Jifu, from a director in the Secretariat, was cast off to a distant place; only after more than ten years did he return, and at once he entered the inner precincts; now it has been barely a year, and among the rising talents I have scarcely made acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: He told Ji, "After exile from a Secretariat post I wandered more than ten years before returning straight into the inner court. I have been back only a year and scarcely know the younger talents.

sentences.zh: 宰相之職，宜選擢賢俊，今則懵然莫知能否。

translations.literal: The office of chancellor ought to select and promote the worthy; now I am benighted and do not know who is capable.
translations.idiomatic: A chancellor should elevate the able, yet I am in the dark about who can serve.

sentences.zh: 卿多精鑒，今之才傑，為我言之。」

translations.literal: You are skilled in discernment; tell me of the outstanding talents of today."
translations.idiomatic: You have a keen eye—name the outstanding men of our day for me."

sentences.zh: 垍取筆疏其名氏，得三十餘人。

translations.literal: Ji took up the brush and listed their names, obtaining more than thirty men.
translations.idiomatic: Ji wrote out more than thirty names at his dictation.

sentences.zh: 數月之內，選用略盡，當時翕然稱吉甫有得人之稱。

translations.literal: Within a few months the selections were largely exhausted, and at the time all agreed in praising Jifu for having the reputation of gaining men.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he had appointed nearly all of them, and contemporaries widely praised Jifu for knowing how to choose talent.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔舉賢良，時有皇甫湜對策，其言激切；

translations.literal: In the third year an edict summoned the worthy; at that time Huangfu Shi submitted a policy essay, his words sharp and cutting;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the court called for worthy men; Huangfu Shi's policy response was fiercely blunt;

sentences.zh: 牛僧孺、李宗閔亦苦詆時政。

translations.literal: Niu Sengru and Li Zongmin also bitterly denounced current policy.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru and Li Zongmin likewise assailed the government in harsh terms.

sentences.zh: 考官楊於陵、韋貫之升三子之策皆上第，垍居中覆視，無所同異。

translations.literal: The examiners Yang Yuling and Wei Guanzhi ranked all three candidates' essays in the top grade; Ji reviewed them in the middle and found no discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Examiners Yang Yuling and Wei Guanzhi placed all three in the top tier; Ji's review as chief examiner found no reason to disagree.

sentences.zh: 及為貴幸泣訴，請罪於上，憲宗不得已，出於陵、貫之官，罷垍翰林學士，除戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When favored courtiers wept and pleaded, begging punishment from the throne, Emperor Xianzong had no choice but to remove Yang Yuling and Wei Guanzhi from office, dismiss Ji as Hanlin academician, and appoint him Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Favored courtiers wept before the emperor and demanded punishment; Xianzong reluctantly ousted Yang and Wei from office, stripped Ji of his Hanlin post, and made him Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 然憲宗知垍好直，信任彌厚。

translations.literal: Yet Xianzong knew Ji loved uprightness, and his trust grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xianzong knew Ji prized integrity, and trusted him all the more.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，李吉甫出鎮淮南，遂以垍代為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: That autumn Li Jifu went out to command Huainan, and Ji was appointed in his stead as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Li Jifu took command in Huainan, and Ji replaced him as Secretariat vice director and associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 明年，加集賢院大學士、監修國史。

translations.literal: The next year he was additionally made Grand Academician of the Jixian Institute and supervisor of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was also named grand academician of the Jixian Institute and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 垍奏：「集賢御書院，請準《六典》，登朝官五品已上為學士，六品已下為直學士；

translations.literal: Ji memorialized: "For the Jixian Imperial Library, please follow the Six Institutions: court officials of the fifth rank and above shall be academicians, those of the sixth rank and below shall be direct academicians;
translations.idiomatic: Ji submitted: "For the Jixian Imperial Library, follow the Six Institutions: court officials of fifth rank and above should be academicians, sixth rank and below direct academicians;

sentences.zh: 自非登朝官，不問品秩，並為校理；

translations.literal: if not court officials, regardless of rank, all shall be collators;
translations.idiomatic: anyone not a court official, whatever rank, should be a collator;

sentences.zh: 其餘名目一切勒停。

translations.literal: all other titles are to be abolished entirely.
translations.idiomatic: and all other titles abolished outright.

sentences.zh: 史館請登朝官入館者，並為修撰；

translations.literal: For the History Office, court officials who enter the office shall all be compilers;
translations.idiomatic: At the History Office, court officials admitted to the institute shall all be compilers;

sentences.zh: 非登朝官，並為直史館。

translations.literal: those who are not court officials shall all be direct historians of the office.
translations.idiomatic: non-court officials shall all be direct historians of the office.

sentences.zh: 仍永為常式。」

translations.literal: Let this remain a permanent regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Let this stand as permanent practice.

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved it all.

sentences.zh: 元和五年，中風病。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanhe he suffered a wind stroke.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 5 he suffered a stroke.

sentences.zh: 憲宗甚嗟惜，中使旁午致問，至於藥膳進退，皆令疏陳。

translations.literal: Xianzong deeply lamented it; palace envoys came and went in succession with inquiries, and even regarding medicine, food, and comings and goings he ordered memorials of detail.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was deeply distressed; eunuch envoys called incessantly, and even his medicines and meals were to be reported in writing.

sentences.zh: 疾益痼，罷為兵部尚書，仍進階銀青。

translations.literal: The illness grew chronic; he was removed as Minister of War, yet still advanced in rank to silver and cyan.
translations.idiomatic: As the illness worsened he was relieved as Minister of War but promoted in rank to silver and cyan.

sentences.zh: 明年，改太子賓客。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，廢朝，賻禮有加，贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: He died; court was suspended; funeral gifts were increased; he was posthumously made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died; the court suspended audience; funeral gifts were augmented; he was posthumously named Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 初，垍在翰林承旨，屬憲宗初平吳、蜀，勵精思理，機密之務，一以關垍。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ji was chief Hanlin academician, as Xianzong had just pacified Wu and Shu and was striving to govern diligently, all confidential affairs were entrusted entirely to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as chief Hanlin academician after Xianzong's pacification of Wu and Shu, he entrusted every confidential matter to Ji while striving to govern.

sentences.zh: 垍小心敬慎，甚稱中旨。

translations.literal: Ji was careful and reverent, and greatly accorded with the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was meticulous and reverent, and fully satisfied the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 及作相之後，懇請旌別淑慝，杜絕蹊徑，齊整法度，考課吏理，皆蒙垂意聽納。

translations.literal: After he became chancellor, his earnest pleas to distinguish good from evil, cut off bypaths, align regulations, and examine officials' governance all received the emperor's attentive acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor his pleas to reward virtue and punish vice, close back doors, tighten law, and grade officials' performance all won the emperor's heed.

sentences.zh: 吐突承璀自春宮侍憲宗，恩顧莫二。

translations.literal: Tutu Chenghuan had attended Xianzong since the Eastern Palace, and no one else enjoyed such favor.
translations.idiomatic: Tutu Chenghuan had served Xianzong since his days as heir, and enjoyed unrivaled favor.

sentences.zh: 承璀承間欲有所關說，憲宗憚垍，誡勿復言，在禁中常以官呼垍而不名。

translations.literal: Chenghuan seized an opening to make some intercession; Xianzong feared Ji and warned him not to speak again; within the palace he often called Ji by his office title and not by name.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghuan tried to intervene on someone's behalf; Xianzong, wary of Ji, forbade him to speak further and in the palace often addressed Ji by title rather than name.

sentences.zh: 楊於陵為嶺南節度使，與監軍許遂振不和，遂振誣奏於陵，憲宗令追與慢官。

translations.literal: Yang Yuling was military commissioner of Lingnan; he was at odds with the army supervisor Xu Suizhen, who falsely memorialized against Yuling; Xianzong ordered him recalled and given a demoted post.
translations.idiomatic: As Lingnan commissioner Yang Yuling clashed with army supervisor Xu Suizhen, who slandered him; Xianzong ordered Yang recalled and demoted.

sentences.zh: 垍曰：「以遂振故罪一籓臣，不可。」

translations.literal: Ji said: "To punish a frontier minister because of Suizhen is unacceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "We cannot punish a frontier minister on Suizhen's account.

sentences.zh: 請授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He requested that Yang be given the post of Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Yang be made Vice Minister of Personnel instead.

sentences.zh: 嚴綬在太原，其政事一出監軍李輔光，綬但拱手而已，垍具奏其事，請以李鄘代之。

translations.literal: Yan Shou was at Taiyuan; all administration issued from the army supervisor Li Fuguang, and Shou merely folded his hands; Ji fully memorialized the matter and asked that Li Yong replace him.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan Yan Shou let army supervisor Li Fuguang run everything while he stood idle; Ji reported this in full and asked that Li Yong replace him.

sentences.zh: 王士真死，其子承宗以河北故事請代父為帥。

translations.literal: Wang Shizhen died; his son Chengzong, citing Hebei precedent, asked to succeed his father as commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shizhen died, his son Chengzong invoked Hebei custom to succeed him as military governor.

sentences.zh: 憲宗意速於太平，且頻蕩寇孽，謂其地可取。

translations.literal: Xianzong's mind was quick toward peace, and having repeatedly swept away rebel bands, he thought the territory could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Eager for peace and having crushed rebels repeatedly, Xianzong thought the region could be seized.

sentences.zh: 吐突承璀恃恩，謀撓垍權，遂伺君意，請自征討。

translations.literal: Tutu Chenghuan relied on favor and plotted to undermine Ji's power; he then watched the sovereign's intent and asked to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: Tutu Chenghuan, trusting his favor, sought to undercut Ji and, reading the emperor's mood, volunteered to lead the campaign himself.

sentences.zh: 盧從史陰苞逆節，內與承宗相結約，而外請興師，以圖厚利。

translations.literal: Lu Congshi secretly harbored rebellious designs, inwardly made a pact with Chengzong, yet outwardly asked to raise troops, seeking great profit.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi secretly nursed treason, allied with Chengzong within, yet outwardly urged war to reap rich gains.

sentences.zh: 垍一一陳其不可，且言：「武俊有大功於朝，前授李師道而後奪承宗，是賞罰不一，無以沮勸天下。」

translations.literal: Ji set forth one by one why it could not be done, and said: "Wujun rendered great service to the court; first Li Shidao was granted command and then Chengzong was denied—this is inconsistent reward and punishment, and cannot deter or encourage the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Ji laid out each objection and said, "Wang Wujun served the throne greatly; we first gave Li Shidao a command, then would deny Chengzong—rewards and punishments would be inconsistent and the realm could neither be warned nor encouraged."

sentences.zh: 逗留半歲，憲宗不決，承璀之策竟行。

translations.literal: They lingered half a year; Xianzong could not decide; Chenghuan's plan was carried out in the end.
translations.idiomatic: For half a year the court hesitated; in the end Chenghuan's plan prevailed.

sentences.zh: 及師臨賊境，從史果攜貳，承璀數督戰，從史益驕倨反覆，官軍病之。

translations.literal: When the army reached the rebel border, Congshi indeed wavered in loyalty; Chenghuan repeatedly pressed for battle; Congshi grew ever more arrogant, perverse, and changeable, and the imperial army suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached the enemy frontier Congshi proved disloyal; Chenghuan kept pressing attacks while Congshi grew arrogant and erratic, to the army's dismay.

sentences.zh: 時王師久暴露無功，上意亦怠。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial army had long been exposed in the field without success, and the emperor's will also slackened.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial forces had campaigned long without victory, and the emperor's ardor cooled.

sentences.zh: 後從史遣其衙門將王翊元入奏，垍延與語，微動其心，且喻以為臣之節，翊元因吐誠言從史惡稔可圖之狀。

translations.literal: Later Congshi sent his yamen general Wang Yiyuan to present a memorial; Ji detained him for conversation, subtly moved his heart, and instructed him in the duty of a subject; Yiyuan then spoke frankly of how Congshi's evil was ripe and could be plotted against.
translations.idiomatic: Later Congshi sent his staff general Wang Yiyuan to court; Ji drew him into talk, stirred his conscience, and taught him a subject's duty; Yiyuan then revealed that Congshi's crimes were ripe and could be seized.

sentences.zh: 垍遣再往，比復還，遂得其大將烏重胤等要領。

translations.literal: Ji sent him back again; when he returned, they thus obtained the vital points from his great generals Wu Chongyin and others.
translations.idiomatic: Ji sent him back a second time, and on his return secured the cooperation of Congshi's chief generals, including Wu Chongyin.

sentences.zh: 垍因從容啟言：「從史暴戾，有無君之心。

translations.literal: Ji then calmly opened his speech: "Congshi is violent and cruel and has a heart that disowns the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Ji then said calmly, "Congshi is brutal and harbors disloyal intent.

sentences.zh: 今聞其視承璀如嬰孩，往來神策壁壘間，益自恃不嚴，是天亡之時也。

translations.literal: Now I hear he treats Chenghuan like an infant, coming and going among the Shence ramparts, growing ever more reliant and lax in guard—this is the time Heaven will destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: He treats Chenghuan like a child, wanders among the Shence camps unguarded, and grows reckless—Heaven's hour to destroy him has come.

sentences.zh: 若不因其機而致之，後雖興師，未可以歲月破也。」

translations.literal: If we do not seize him by this opportunity, later even if we raise armies, we may not break him within months and years."
translations.idiomatic: If we miss this chance, even another campaign may not break him for years.

sentences.zh: 憲宗初愕然，熟思其計，方許之。

translations.literal: Xianzong was at first startled, pondered the plan deeply, and then assented.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was startled at first, weighed the plan, and then agreed.

sentences.zh: 垍因請密其謀，憲宗曰：「此唯李絳、梁守謙知之。」

translations.literal: Ji then asked that the plot be kept secret; Xianzong said: "Only Li Jiang and Liang Shouqian shall know of this."
translations.idiomatic: Ji asked that the plot be kept secret; Xianzong said, "Only Li Jiang and Liang Shouqian may know.

sentences.zh: 時絳承旨翰林，守謙掌密命。

translations.literal: At that time Jiang was chief Hanlin academician, and Shouqian held confidential orders.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was then chief Hanlin academician and Shouqian held confidential orders.

sentences.zh: 後承璀竟擒從史，平上黨，其年秋班師。

translations.literal: Later Chenghuan indeed captured Congshi and pacified Shangdang; that autumn the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghuan later captured Congshi and pacified Shangdang; that autumn the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 垍以「承璀首唱用兵，今還無功，陛下縱念舊勞，不能加顯戮，亦請貶黜以謝天下」。

translations.literal: Ji submitted that "Chenghuan was the first to urge the use of troops; now he returns without merit; even if Your Majesty recalls old service and cannot impose open punishment, still please demote him to answer the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Ji argued that Chenghuan had first urged war yet returned without merit; even if the emperor spared him capital punishment for old service, he should still be demoted to satisfy the realm.

sentences.zh: 遂罷承璀兵柄。

translations.literal: Chenghuan's military authority was then removed.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghuan was then stripped of military command.

sentences.zh: 先是，天下百姓輸賦於州府：一曰上供，二曰送使，三曰留州。

translations.literal: Earlier, the common people throughout the realm paid taxes to the prefectures: first, tribute to the center; second, delivery to commissioners; third, retention by the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the people paid taxes to their prefectures in three shares: tribute to the capital, delivery to commissioners, and retention by the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建中初定兩稅，時貸重錢輕；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong the two-tax system was fixed; then goods were heavy and cash light;
translations.idiomatic: When the two-tax system was established early in Jianzhong, goods were dear and cash cheap;

sentences.zh: 是後貨輕錢重，齊人所出，固已倍其初征。

translations.literal: afterward goods were light and cash heavy, and what the people of Qi paid had already doubled the initial levy.
translations.idiomatic: later goods grew cheap and cash dear, so what households paid had already doubled the original levy.

sentences.zh: 而其留州送使，所在長吏又降省估使就實估，以自封殖而重賦於人。

translations.literal: Yet for what was retained by the prefecture and delivered to commissioners, local chief officials further lowered the official estimate and forced payment at the true estimate, enriching themselves and imposing heavy levies on the people.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials then discounted official valuations and collected at market rates on retained and delivered shares, enriching themselves while burdening the people.

sentences.zh: 及垍為相，奏請：「天下留州、送使物，一切令依省估。

translations.literal: When Ji became chancellor he memorialized: "For all goods retained by prefectures and delivered to commissioners throughout the realm, let everything follow the official estimate.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor Ji petitioned that all retained and delivered goods empire-wide follow the official estimate.

sentences.zh: 其所在觀察使，仍以其所蒞之郡租賦自給；

translations.literal: The observation commissioners in each region shall still support themselves from the tax revenues of the commanderies they oversee;
translations.idiomatic: Observation commissioners should still fund themselves from the taxes of the prefectures they oversee;

sentences.zh: 若不足，然後征於支郡。」

translations.literal: if insufficient, only then levy from subordinate commanderies."
translations.idiomatic: and only if that fell short levy subordinate prefectures.

sentences.zh: 其諸州送使額，悉變為上供，故江淮稍息肩。

translations.literal: The quotas for delivery to commissioners in the various prefectures all became tribute to the center, and thus the Jiang-Huai region slightly eased its shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: Delivery quotas from the prefectures were converted to central tribute, bringing modest relief to the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 垍雖年少，驟居相位，而器局峻整，有法度，雖大僚前輩，其造請不敢幹以私。

translations.literal: Although Ji was young and had suddenly attained the chancellorship, his bearing was stern and orderly and he had standards; even senior great officials did not dare press private requests on his visits.
translations.idiomatic: Though young and suddenly elevated to chancellor, Ji was stern and principled; even senior ministers dared not press private favors when they called.

sentences.zh: 諫官言時政得失，舊事，操權者多不悅其舉職。

translations.literal: When remonstrance officials spoke of the gains and losses of current policy, it was the old practice; those who wielded power often disliked their fulfillment of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials had long spoken on policy's strengths and flaws, yet men in power often resented their diligence.

sentences.zh: 垍在中書，有獨孤郁、李正辭、嚴休復自拾遺轉補闕，及參謝之際，垍廷語之曰：「獨孤與李二補闕，孜孜獻納，今之遷轉，可謂酬勞愧矣。

translations.literal: When Ji was in the Secretariat, Dugu Yu, Li Zhengc, and Yan Xiufu were transferred from remonstrator to supplementer; at their audience of thanks Ji addressed them in court and said: "The two supplementers Dugu and Li have diligently offered remonstrance; today's transfer may be called a reward for labor that shames me.
translations.idiomatic: In the Secretariat Dugu Yu, Li Zhengc, and Yan Xiufu were promoted from remonstrator to supplementer; at their thanks audience Ji said in open court, "Dugu and Li have remonstrated tirelessly; this promotion is a reward that shames me.

sentences.zh: 嚴補闕官業，或異於斯，昨者進擬，不無疑緩。」

translations.literal: Supplementer Yan's official conduct may differ from this; yesterday's proposed advancement was not without hesitation and delay."
translations.idiomatic: Supplementer Yan's conduct may differ; yesterday's nomination was not without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 休復悚恧而退。

translations.literal: Xiufu withdrew in fear and shame.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufu withdrew, abashed.

sentences.zh: 垍在翰林，舉李絳、崔群同掌密命；

translations.literal: In the Hanlin Ji recommended Li Jiang and Cui Qun to share charge of confidential edicts;
translations.idiomatic: In the Hanlin he recommended Li Jiang and Cui Qun to share confidential edicts;

sentences.zh: 及在相位，用韋貫之、裴度知制誥，擢李夷簡為御史中丞，其後繼踵入相，鹹著名跡。

translations.literal: when he reached the chancellorship he employed Wei Guanzhi and Pei Du as drafters of edicts, promoted Li Yijian to censor-in-chief, and afterward they followed one another into the chancellorship, all leaving renowned traces.
translations.idiomatic: as chancellor he used Wei Guanzhi and Pei Du as edict drafters, raised Li Yijian to chief censor, and each later entered the chancellorship with distinguished records.

sentences.zh: 其余量材賦職，皆葉人望，選任之精，前後莫及。

translations.literal: The rest he assigned posts according to talent, all meeting public expectation; the fineness of selection before and after could not be matched.
translations.idiomatic: His other appointments matched talent to office and public expectation; none before or since matched the precision of his selections.

sentences.zh: 議者謂垍作相，才與時會，知無不為，於時朝無幸人，百度浸理；

translations.literal: Commentators said that when Ji served as chancellor, talent met the times, and wherever he knew he acted; at that time the court had no favorites, and the hundred offices gradually were put in order;
translations.idiomatic: Observers said that as chancellor Ji's talent met the moment and he left nothing undone; the court had no favorites and government gradually righted itself;

sentences.zh: 而再周遘疾，以至休謝，公論惜之。

translations.literal: yet within two cycles illness came, leading to withdrawal from office, and public opinion lamented it.
translations.idiomatic: yet within two years illness forced his retirement, to public regret.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫，字弘憲，趙郡人。

translations.literal: Li Jifu, style Hongxian, was a man of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu, styled Hongxian, was from Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 父棲筠，代宗朝為御史大夫，名重於時，國史有傳。

translations.literal: His father Qiyun served as censor-in-chief in the Daizong reign and was renowned in his time; the national history has his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Qiyun had been censor-in-chief under Daizong and was celebrated in his day; the national history records him.

sentences.zh: 吉甫少好學，能屬文。

translations.literal: Jifu from youth loved learning and could compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu loved learning from youth and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 年二十七，為太常博士，該洽多聞，尤精國朝故實，沿革折衷，時多稱之。

translations.literal: At twenty-seven he became a doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, comprehensive and widely informed, especially expert in the institutions and precedents of the dynasty, weighing origins and changes; many praised him at the time.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-seven he became a Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, erudite and especially versed in dynastic precedent; contemporaries praised him widely.

sentences.zh: 遷屯田員外郎，博士如故，改駕部員外。

translations.literal: He was transferred to assistant director of the Directorate of Agriculture, retaining his doctorate, then changed to assistant director of the Directorate of Equipage.
translations.idiomatic: He was made assistant director of agriculture while keeping his doctorate, then transferred to assistant director of equipage.

sentences.zh: 宰臣李泌、竇參推重其才，接遇頗厚。

translations.literal: Chancellors Li Bi and Dou Can esteemed his talent and treated him with considerable warmth.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Li Bi and Dou Can valued his talent and received him warmly.

sentences.zh: 及陸贄為相，出為明州員外長史；

translations.literal: When Lu Zhi became chancellor, Jifu was sent out as senior adjutant of Ming prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Zhi became chancellor, Jifu was posted out as senior adjutant at Mingzhou;

sentences.zh: 久之遇赦，起為忠州刺史。

translations.literal: after a long while he met an amnesty and was recalled as prefect of Zhong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he was recalled on amnesty as prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時贄已謫在忠州，議者謂吉甫必逞憾於贄，重構其罪；

translations.literal: At that time Zhi had already been banished to Zhong prefecture; commentators said Jifu would surely vent old resentment on Zhi and fabricate new crimes against him;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi was already exiled to Zhongzhou; observers expected Jifu to settle old scores and fabricate new charges;

sentences.zh: 及吉甫到部，與贄甚歡，未嘗以宿嫌介意。

translations.literal: when Jifu reached his post he was on very cordial terms with Zhi and never minded their old enmity.
translations.idiomatic: but when Jifu arrived they were on excellent terms and he never brooded over past grievances.

sentences.zh: 六年不徙官，以疾罷免。

translations.literal: For six years he was not transferred; he was dismissed because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Six years passed without transfer before illness forced his retirement.

sentences.zh: 尋授柳州刺史，遷饒州。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Liuzhou, then transferred to Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Liuzhou, then transferred to Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，州城以頻喪四牧，廢而不居，物怪變異，郡人信驗；

translations.literal: Earlier, because four prefects in succession had died, the prefectural city was abandoned and uninhabited; strange things and transformations occurred, and the people of the commandery believed and verified them;
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural seat had been abandoned after four successive prefects died there; omens and strange events convinced the locals;

sentences.zh: 吉甫至，發城門管鑰，剪荊榛而居之，後人乃安。

translations.literal: When Jifu arrived he opened the city gates and keys, cut the brambles and thorns, and dwelt there; afterward people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu opened the gates, cleared the thorn scrub, and moved in; afterward the people were reassured.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嗣位，征拜考功郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: When Xianzong succeeded to the throne, Jifu was summoned and appointed director of examinations and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong ascended the throne, Jifu was summoned as director of examinations with charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 既至闕下，旋召入翰林為學士，轉中書舍人，賜紫。

translations.literal: Once he reached the capital he was soon called into the Hanlin as academician, transferred to Secretariat drafter, and granted purple.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he was soon made Hanlin academician, then Secretariat drafter, and granted purple robes.

sentences.zh: 憲宗初即位，中書小吏滑渙與知樞密中使劉光琦暱善，頗竊朝權，吉甫請去之。

translations.literal: When Xianzong had just taken the throne, the Secretariat clerk Hua Huan and the eunuch Liu Guangqi, who knew the privy council, were intimate and friendly and greatly usurped court power; Jifu asked that they be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianzong's reign Secretariat clerk Hua Huan and privy-council eunuch Liu Guangqi were close allies who usurped court power; Jifu asked that they be removed.

sentences.zh: 劉闢反，帝命誅討之；

translations.literal: Liu Pi rebelled; the emperor ordered him punished and suppressed;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi rebelled, the emperor ordered his suppression;

sentences.zh: 計未決，吉甫密贊其謀，兼請廣征江淮之師，由三峽路入，以分蜀寇之力。

translations.literal: the plan was undecided; Jifu secretly supported the scheme and also asked to raise troops broadly from the Jiang-Huai, entering by the Three Gorges route to divide the strength of the Shu rebels.
translations.idiomatic: while the plan was still unsettled Jifu secretly backed it and urged raising Jiang-Huai forces to enter through the Three Gorges and divide the Shu rebels' strength.

sentences.zh: 事皆允從，由是甚見親信。

translations.literal: All matters were approved, and from this he was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: All was approved, and from then on he enjoyed deep trust.

sentences.zh: 二年春，杜黃裳出鎮，擢吉甫為中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year Du Huangshang went out to command a region, and Jifu was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year, when Du Huangshang took a frontier command, Jifu was promoted to Secretariat vice director and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 吉甫性聰敏，詳練物務，自員外郎出官，留滯江淮十五餘年，備詳閭裏疾苦。

translations.literal: Jifu was by nature clever and keen, thorough and practiced in worldly affairs; from assistant director he went out to office and lingered in the Jiang-Huai more than fifteen years, fully knowing the hardships of village and lane.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and practiced in affairs, Jifu had spent more than fifteen years in the Jiang-Huai after leaving the capital and knew the people's hardships intimately.

sentences.zh: 及是為相，患方鎮貪恣，乃上言使屬郡刺史得自為政。

translations.literal: When he became chancellor he worried over the greed and license of the regional commands and memorialized that prefects of subordinate commanderies should govern on their own.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor he deplored the greed of military governors and urged that subordinate prefects govern independently.

sentences.zh: 敘進群材，甚有美稱。

translations.literal: He advanced many talents in order and enjoyed a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted talent widely and won high praise.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，裴均為僕射、判度支，交結權幸，欲求宰相。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year Pei Jun was Vice Director of the Secretariat and chief of the Treasury, associating with the powerful and favored, and sought to become chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Pei Jun, as vice director and treasury chief, courted the powerful and sought the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 先是，制策試直言極諫科，其中有譏刺時政，忤犯權幸者，因此均黨揚言皆執政教指，冀以搖動吉甫，賴諫官李約、獨孤郁、李正辭、蕭俛密疏陳奏，帝意乃解。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the decree examination for Outspoken Remonstrance, some answers satirized current policy and offended the powerful; therefore Jun's faction spread word that all were directed by the administration, hoping to shake Jifu; thanks to remonstrance officials Li Yue, Dugu Yu, Li Zhengc, and Xiao Fu, who secretly memorialized, the emperor's mind was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: When the outspoken-remonstrance examination produced answers that attacked policy and offended favorites, Jun's faction claimed Jifu had orchestrated them; remonstrators Li Yue, Dugu Yu, Li Zhengc, and Xiao Fu secretly clarified matters and eased the emperor's suspicions.

sentences.zh: 吉甫早歲知獎羊士諤，擢為監察御史；

translations.literal: Jifu in his early years recognized and rewarded Yang Shiyu and promoted him to investigating censor;
translations.idiomatic: Jifu had early favored Yang Shiyu and made him an investigating censor;

sentences.zh: 又司封員外郎呂溫有詞藝，吉甫亦眷接之。

translations.literal: also the assistant director of Seals Lü Wen had literary skill, and Jifu likewise favored and received him.
translations.idiomatic: and he also favored Lü Wen, an assistant director of Seals noted for literary skill.

sentences.zh: 竇群亦與羊、呂善。

translations.literal: Dou Qun was also on good terms with Yang and Lü.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Qun was likewise close to Yang and Lü.

sentences.zh: 群初拜御史中丞，奏請士諤為侍御史，溫為郎中、知雜事。

translations.literal: When Qun was first appointed censor-in-chief he memorialized asking that Shiyu be attendant censor and Wen director with charge of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On becoming censor-in-chief, Qun asked that Shiyu be attendant censor and Wen a director in charge of miscellaneous business.

sentences.zh: 吉甫怒其不先關白，而所請又有超資者，持之數日不行，因而有隙。

translations.literal: Jifu was angry that he had not informed him beforehand and that some requests exceeded qualifications; he held them several days without action, and thus a rift arose.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu was angered that Qun had not consulted him first and sought overqualified appointments; he stalled the requests for days, and a breach opened between them.

sentences.zh: 群遂伺得日者陳克明出入吉甫家，密捕以聞；

translations.literal: Qun then watched until he found the day-selector Chen Keming entering and leaving Jifu's house and secretly arrested and reported him;
translations.idiomatic: Qun then caught the day-selector Chen Keming visiting Jifu's house and secretly arrested and reported him;

sentences.zh: 憲宗詰之，無奸狀。

translations.literal: Xianzong interrogated the matter and found no treacherous circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong investigated and found no wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 吉甫以裴垍久在翰林，憲宗親信，必當大用，遂密薦垍代己，因自圖出鎮。

translations.literal: Jifu, because Pei Ji had long been in the Hanlin and Xianzong trusted him closely and would surely be greatly used, secretly recommended Ji to replace himself and thus plotted to go out and command a region.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Pei Ji, long trusted in the Hanlin, was bound for high office, Jifu secretly recommended him as his successor and planned to take a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，拜檢校兵部尚書，兼中書侍郎、平章事，充淮南節度使，上御通化門樓餞之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year he was appointed acting Minister of War, concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, and military commissioner of Huainan; the emperor attended the Tonghua Gate tower to give him a farewell feast.
translations.idiomatic: That September he was made acting Minister of War, grand councilor, and Huainan commissioner; the emperor saw him off from the Tonghua Gate tower.

sentences.zh: 在揚州，每有朝廷得失，軍國利害，皆密疏論列。

translations.literal: At Yangzhou, whenever there were gains or losses at court or advantages or harms to army and state, he all secretly memorialized and set them forth.
translations.idiomatic: From Yangzhou he sent secret memorials on every court matter and military concern of consequence.

sentences.zh: 又於高郵縣築堤為塘，溉田數千頃，人受其惠。

translations.literal: He also built dikes into ponds at Gaoyou County, irrigating several thousand qing of fields; the people received the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He also built dikes and ponds at Gaoyou that irrigated thousands of acres, to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，裴垍病免。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year Pei Ji was dismissed because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the fifth year Pei Ji retired on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，授吉甫金紫光祿大夫、中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿大學士、監修國史、上柱國、趙國公。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Jifu was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall, supervisor of the national history, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month Jifu was made grand councilor, grand academician of Jixian, supervisor of national history, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 及再入相，請減省職員並諸色出身胥吏等，及量定中外官俸料，時以為當。

translations.literal: When he entered the chancellorship again he asked to reduce staff and clerks of various origins, and to measure and fix salaries of central and local officials; contemporaries thought it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to office he sought to cut redundant staff and clerks and to standardize official salaries, which contemporaries judged appropriate.

sentences.zh: 京城諸僧有以莊磑免稅者，吉甫奏曰：「錢米所征，素有定額，寬緇徒有餘之力，配貧下無告之民，必不可許。」

translations.literal: Monks in the capital had estates and mills exempted from tax; Jifu memorialized: "Cash and grain levied have long had fixed quotas; to spare the surplus strength of the black-robed and assign it to the poor without recourse is absolutely not permissible."
translations.idiomatic: When capital monks sought tax exemption for estates and mills, Jifu argued that fixed quotas could not be relaxed for clerics at the expense of the destitute.

sentences.zh: 憲宗乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor Xianzong thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then stopped it.

sentences.zh: 又請歸普潤軍於涇原。

translations.literal: He also asked that the Pujun army be returned to Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the Pujun army be reassigned to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 七年，京兆尹元義方奏：「永昌公主準禮令起祠堂，請其制度。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Metropolitan Governor Yuan Yifang memorialized: "Princess Yongchang, following the ritual statutes, is to erect an ancestral hall; we request its regulations."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the metropolitan governor Yuan Yifang reported that Princess Yongchang wished to build a memorial hall according to ritual law and asked what form it should take.

sentences.zh: 初，貞元中，義陽、義章二公主咸於墓所造祠堂一百二十間，費錢數萬；

translations.literal: Early in the Zhenyuan era the Princesses of Yiyang and Yizhang had each built one hundred twenty halls at their tombs, costing tens of thousands in cash;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Zhenyuan era, the Princesses of Yiyang and Yizhang had each built one hundred twenty halls at their tombs at a cost of tens of thousands of strings of cash;

sentences.zh: 及永昌之制，上令義方減舊制之半。

translations.literal: regarding Yongchang's regulations, the emperor ordered Yifang to reduce the old regulations by half.
translations.idiomatic: when Yongchang's case arose, the emperor ordered Yifang to cut the earlier scale in half.

sentences.zh: 吉甫奏曰：「伏以永昌公主，稚年夭枉，舉代同悲，況於聖情，固所鐘念。

translations.literal: Jifu memorialized: "I submit that Princess Yongchang, cut down in tender years, moves the age to shared grief; how much the more is she fixed in the Sacred Heart's care.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu replied that the princess, taken young, grieved the whole realm and was especially dear to the emperor's heart.

sentences.zh: 然陛下猶減制造之半，示折衷之規，昭儉訓人，實越今古。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty still reduced the construction by half, showing a rule of compromise, manifesting frugality to instruct the people — truly surpassing past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty had still halved the scale, showing moderation and teaching frugality — a lesson rare in any age.

sentences.zh: 臣以祠堂之設，禮典無文，德宗皇帝恩出一時，事因習俗，當時人間不無竊議。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that the setting up of ancestral halls has no warrant in the ritual canon; Emperor Dezong's grace issued from the moment, the affair following custom; at the time among the people there was no lack of private criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial halls, I believe, have no basis in the ritual canon; Emperor Dezong's favor was a momentary indulgence following custom, and people at the time whispered against it.

sentences.zh: 昔漢章帝時，欲為光武原陵、明帝顯節陵，各起邑屋，東平王蒼上疏言其不可。

translations.literal: In former times under Han Zhangdi, wishing for Guangwu's Mausoleum at Yuanling and Mingdi's at Xianjieling, to raise walled dwellings for each, the Prince of Dongping, Liu Cang, submitted a memorial that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han Zhangdi, when the court wished to build walled settlements at Guangwu's Yuanling and Mingdi's Xianjieling tombs, the Prince of Dongping, Liu Cang, memorialized against it.

sentences.zh: ——東平王即光武之愛子，明帝之愛弟。

translations.literal: — The Prince of Dongping was Guangwu's beloved son and Mingdi's beloved younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: — The Prince of Dongping was Guangwu's beloved son and Mingdi's beloved younger brother.

sentences.zh: 賢王之心，豈惜費於父兄哉！

translations.literal: Could the worthy prince's heart have grudged expense for father and elder brother!
translations.idiomatic: A prince so worthy would not have begrudged the cost for his father and brother!

sentences.zh: 誠以非禮之事，人君所當慎也。

translations.literal: It was truly because uncanonical affairs are what a ruler ought to treat with caution.
translations.idiomatic: He objected because improper rites are what a ruler must guard against.

sentences.zh: 今者，依義陽公主起祠堂，臣恐不如量置墓戶，以充守奉。」

translations.literal: Now, following the Princess of Yiyang in raising an ancestral hall, your servant fears it would be better to assign tomb households in measure, to supply guarding and maintenance."
translations.idiomatic: To follow the Princess of Yiyang in building a hall, I fear, is inferior to assigning tomb households in suitable number to maintain the grave.

sentences.zh: 翌日，上謂吉甫曰：「卿昨所奏罷祠堂事，深愜朕心。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor said to Jifu: "What you yesterday memorialized on abolishing the ancestral hall deeply suits Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor told Jifu that his memorial to abolish the hall had deeply pleased him.

sentences.zh: 朕初疑其冗費，緣未知故實，是以量減。

translations.literal: We at first doubted its redundant expense; because We did not know the former facts, We therefore reduced it in measure.
translations.idiomatic: I had first suspected waste and, not knowing the precedent, had only trimmed the scale.

sentences.zh: 覽卿所陳，方知無據。

translations.literal: On reading what you set forth, We now know there is no basis.
translations.idiomatic: After reading your argument, I see there was no proper basis at all.

sentences.zh: 然朕不欲破二十戶百姓，當揀官戶委之。」

translations.literal: Yet We do not wish to disrupt twenty households of the common people; We should select official households and assign them."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I do not wish to displace twenty common households; official households should be chosen for the duty instead.

sentences.zh: 吉甫拜賀。

translations.literal: Jifu bowed in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu bowed his thanks.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿，此豈是難事！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Sir, is this a hard thing!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Sir, is that so difficult!

sentences.zh: 有關朕身，不便於時者，茍聞之則改，此豈足多耶！

translations.literal: Where it concerns Our person and is inconvenient for the times, if We hear it We change it — how is this worthy of much praise!
translations.idiomatic: Whatever touches me or ill suits the times, if I hear of it I change it — why make so much of this!

sentences.zh: 卿但勤匡正，無謂朕不能行也。」

translations.literal: You need only diligently set things right; do not suppose that We cannot act."
translations.idiomatic: Keep advising me faithfully; do not think I cannot follow your counsel."

sentences.zh: 七年七月，上御延英，顧謂吉甫曰：「朕近日畋遊悉廢，唯喜讀書。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year the emperor held court at Yanying and, turning, said to Jifu: "We have lately abandoned hunting entirely and delight only in reading.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventh year, at Yanying, the emperor turned to Jifu and said he had given up hunting and now read constantly.

sentences.zh: 昨於《代宗實錄》中，見其時綱紀未振，朝廷多事，亦有所鑒誡。

translations.literal: Yesterday in the Veritable Records of Daizong We saw that at that time discipline was unsettled and the court had many affairs — also matter for warning and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, in the Veritable Records of Daizong, I saw how discipline had failed and the court was beset — a warning worth heeding.

sentences.zh: 向後見卿先人事跡，深可嘉嘆。」

translations.literal: Later We saw the deeds and traces of your late father and deeply admired them."
translations.idiomatic: Later I came upon your father's career and was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 吉甫降階跪奏曰：「臣先父伏事代宗，盡心盡節，迫於流運，不待聖時，臣之血誠，常所追恨。

translations.literal: Jifu descended the steps, knelt, and memorialized: "Your servant's late father served Daizong with full heart and full loyalty; constrained by the turning of fortune, he did not await the sacred age — your servant's heartfelt devotion is constantly recalled with regret.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu stepped down, knelt, and said his father had served Daizong with utter loyalty but died before this reign; the son had long grieved that devotion could not be fulfilled in his own time.

sentences.zh: 陛下耽悅文史，聽覽日新，見臣先父忠於前朝，著在實錄，今日特賜褒揚，先父雖在九泉，如睹白日。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty delights in literature and history, your hearing and scrutiny daily renewed; seeing your servant's late father loyal to the former dynasty, recorded in the veritable records, and today especially granted praise — though my late father is in the nine springs, it is as if beholding broad daylight."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty loves letters and learns daily; to see my father's loyalty to the former reign recorded and praised today is for him, though under the earth, as if he saw the sun again.

sentences.zh: 因俯伏流涕，上慰諭之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bowed prone and shed tears; the emperor comforted and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself in tears, and the emperor comforted him.

sentences.zh: 八年十月，上御延英殿，問時政記記何事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year the emperor held court at the Yanying Hall and asked what the Current Affairs Record recorded.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eighth year, at Yanying, the emperor asked what the Current Affairs Record was for.

sentences.zh: 時吉甫監修國史，先對曰：「是宰相記天子事以授史官之實錄也。

translations.literal: Jifu was then supervisor of the national history and answered first: "It is the veritable record in which chancellors record the Son of Heaven's affairs to hand to the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu, who supervised the national history, answered first that it was the chancellors' record of the emperor's affairs for the historiographers.

sentences.zh: 古者，右史記言，今起居舍人是；

translations.literal: In antiquity the right scribe recorded words — today that is the Diarist of Attendance;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the right scribe recorded words; today that is the diarist of attendance;

sentences.zh: 左史記事，今起居郎是。

translations.literal: the left scribe recorded affairs — today that is the Gentleman of Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: the left scribe recorded affairs; today that is the gentleman of attendance.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，宰相姚璹監修國史，慮造膝之言，或不可聞，因請隨奏對而記於仗下，以授於史官，今時政記是也。」

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era Chancellor Yao Guan supervised the national history, fearing that words spoken at knee's distance might not all be heard; he therefore asked to record along with imperial answers beneath the halberds and hand them to the historiographers — today's Current Affairs Record is that."
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui, Chancellor Yao Guan, supervising the history, feared that intimate counsel might not reach the scribes and asked to note answers given at audience beneath the halberds for the historiographers — the origin of today's record.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「間或不修，何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "At times it is not kept up — why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why it was sometimes neglected.

sentences.zh: 曰：「面奉德音，未及施行，總謂機密，故不可書以送史官；

translations.literal: He said: "Commands received in person, not yet put into effect, are altogether deemed secret; therefore they cannot be written and sent to the historiographers;
translations.idiomatic: He said that orders received in person but not yet enacted were treated as secret and could not be written for the historiographers;

sentences.zh: 其間有謀議出於臣下者，又不可自書以付史官；

translations.literal: among them are counsels and discussions arising from ministers, which again cannot be written by oneself and given to the historiographers;
translations.idiomatic: nor could ministers write down their own deliberations for the scribes;

sentences.zh: 及已行者，制令昭然，天下皆得聞知，即史官之記，不待書以授也。

translations.literal: as for what has already been carried out, decrees and orders are manifest, all under Heaven may hear and know — that is the historiographers' record and need not await writing to hand over.
translations.idiomatic: once measures were enacted, the edicts were public and the historiographers needed no separate transcript.

sentences.zh: 且臣觀時政記者，姚璹修之於長壽，及璹罷而事寢；

translations.literal: Moreover your servant observes the Current Affairs Record: Yao Guan compiled it during Changshou; when Guan left office the affair lapsed;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the record was kept when Yao Guan compiled it under Changshou and lapsed when he left office;

sentences.zh: 賈耽、齊抗修之於貞元，及耽、抗罷而事廢。

translations.literal: Jia Dan and Qi Kang compiled it in the Zhenyuan era; when Dan and Kang left office the affair was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan and Qi Kang kept it in Zhenyuan, and it was abandoned when they departed.

sentences.zh: 然則關時政化者，不虛美，不隱惡，謂之良史也。」

translations.literal: Thus what concerns the politics and transforming influence of the age — not falsely praising, not concealing wrong — is called a good history."
translations.idiomatic: What truly governs the age is history that neither flatters nor conceals—that alone deserves the name of a good record."

sentences.zh: 是月，回紇部落南過磧，取西城柳谷路討吐蕃。

translations.literal: That month a Uyghur tribe passed south over the desert, taking the Willow Valley road of the western regions to campaign against Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: That month a Uyghur tribe crossed the desert southward and took the western Willow Valley route against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 西城防禦使周懷義表至，朝廷大恐，以為回紇聲言討吐蕃，意是入寇。

translations.literal: The Western Regions defense commissioner Zhou Huaiyi's memorial arrived; the court was greatly alarmed, believing that the Uyghurs, under color of campaigning against Tibet, intended invasion.
translations.idiomatic: When the western defense commissioner Zhou Huaiyi reported in, the court was alarmed, suspecting the Uyghurs' talk of attacking Tibet masked an invasion.

sentences.zh: 吉甫奏曰：「回紇入寇，且當漸絕和事，不應便來犯邊，但須設備，不足為慮。」

translations.literal: Jifu memorialized: "If the Uyghurs were invading, they would meanwhile gradually break off peaceful relations and ought not straightway come to violate the border; we need only make preparations — it is not worth worry."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu argued that invaders would first break off diplomacy and would not strike so abruptly; preparations sufficed and there was little cause for alarm.

sentences.zh: 因請自夏州至天德，復置廢館一十一所，以通緩急。

translations.literal: He therefore asked from Xia Prefecture to Tiande to restore eleven abandoned relay stations for urgent communication.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to reopen eleven abandoned relay posts from Xia to Tiande for urgent dispatches.

sentences.zh: 又請發夏州騎士五百人，營於經略故城，應援驛使，兼護党項。

translations.literal: He also asked to dispatch five hundred Xia cavalry, encamp them at the old site of the Jinglue command, support the courier riders, and also guard the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for five hundred Xia horsemen to camp at the old Jinglue headquarters to support couriers and protect the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 九年，請於經略故城置宥州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he asked to establish You Prefecture at the old Jinglue site.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he asked to re-establish You Prefecture at the old Jinglue site.

sentences.zh: 六胡州以在靈鹽界，開元中廢六州。

translations.literal: The Six Hu prefectures lay within the Ling-Salt border; in the Kaiyuan era the six prefectures were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Hu prefectures had lain on the Ling-Salt frontier and were abolished in Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 曰：「國家舊置宥州，以寬宥為名，領諸降戶。

translations.literal: He said: "The state formerly set up You Prefecture, taking 'lenient pardon' as its name, to oversee the various surrendered households.
translations.idiomatic: He explained that the state had once established You Prefecture — "lenient pardon" — to govern surrendered tribes.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，宥州寄理於經略軍，蓋以地居其中，可以總統蕃部，北以應接天德，南援夏州。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao You Prefecture was administered in abeyance from the Jinglue army, because its land lay in the center and could oversee the frontier tribes, north to link with Tiande and south to aid Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianbao it had been administered from the Jinglue army, centrally placed to command the frontier tribes, linking Tiande to the north and Xia to the south.

sentences.zh: 今經略遙隸靈武，又不置軍鎮，非舊制也。」

translations.literal: Now Jinglue is remotely subordinate to Lingwu and again has no military garrison — not the old system."
translations.idiomatic: Now Jinglue answered remotely to Lingwu with no garrison — not the old arrangement.

sentences.zh: 憲宗從其奏，復置宥州，詔曰：「天寶中宥州寄理於經略軍，寶應已來，因循遂廢。

translations.literal: The Emperor Xianzong followed his memorial and restored You Prefecture; an edict said: "In the Tianbao era You Prefecture was administered from the Jinglue army; since Baoying, through inertia it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong approved and restored You Prefecture, decreeing that since Baoying inertia had let the Tianbao arrangement lapse.

sentences.zh: 由是昆夷屢擾，党項靡依，蕃部之人，撫懷莫及。

translations.literal: Thereby the outer barbarians repeatedly harried, the Tangut had nowhere to rely, and frontier peoples could not be reached by comfort and care.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians raided repeatedly, the Tangut lacked a refuge, and frontier peoples could not be won by kindness.

sentences.zh: 朕方弘遠略，思復舊規，宜於經略軍置宥州，仍為上州，於郭下置延恩縣，為上縣，屬夏綏銀觀察使。」

translations.literal: We are now enlarging distant strategy and think to restore the old rule: You Prefecture should be placed at the Jinglue army, still as a superior prefecture; beneath its wall Yan'en County should be set as a superior county, subordinate to the commissioner of Xia, Sui, Yin, and Guan."
translations.idiomatic: I now pursue a far-reaching policy and will restore the old rule: You Prefecture shall stand at Jinglue as a superior prefecture, with Yan'en County beneath the wall as a superior county under the Xia-Sui-Yin commissioner."

sentences.zh: 淮西節度使吳少陽卒，其子元濟請襲父位。

translations.literal: The Huai-Xi military commissioner Wu Shaoyang died; his son Wu Yuanji asked to inherit his father's post.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai-Xi commissioner Wu Shaoyang died, and his son Wu Yuanji asked to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 吉甫以為淮西內地，不同河朔，且四境無黨援，國家常宿數十萬兵以為守禦，宜因時而取之。

translations.literal: Jifu held that Huai-Xi was interior territory, unlike the Hebei-Shuo frontier, and on all four sides had no factional support; the state commonly kept several hundred thousand troops for defense — it should be taken opportunely.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu held that Huai-Xi lay in the interior, unlike the Hebei frontier, had no allies on its borders, and already cost the state hundreds of thousands of troops to garrison — it should be seized while the moment allowed.

sentences.zh: 頗葉上旨，始為經度淮西之謀。

translations.literal: This considerably diverged from the emperor's intent and began the planning to pacify Huai-Xi.
translations.idiomatic: This ran against the emperor's inclination and opened the plan to pacify Huai-Xi.

sentences.zh: 元和九年冬，暴病卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the winter of the ninth year of Yuanhe he died suddenly of illness, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Yuanhe 9 he died suddenly of illness at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 憲宗傷悼久之，遣中使臨吊；

translations.literal: Xianzong grieved for a long while and sent a palace envoy to mourn on his behalf;
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong mourned him at length and sent a palace envoy to offer condolences;

sentences.zh: 常贈之外，內出絹五百匹以恤其家，再贈司空。

translations.literal: beyond the regular posthumous gifts, the inner palace issued five hundred bolts of silk to comfort his family, and he was again enfeoffed as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: beyond the usual honors the inner palace gave five hundred bolts of silk to his family and posthumously made him Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 吉甫初為相，頗洽時情，及淮南再徵，中外延望風采。

translations.literal: When Jifu first became chancellor he very much suited public sentiment; when he was summoned again from Huainan, court and countryside alike looked forward to his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: When Jifu first took office he won wide approval; on his second summons from Huainan, court and country alike awaited his return.

sentences.zh: 秉政之後，視聽時有所蔽，人心疑憚之。

translations.literal: After he held power, his sight and hearing were at times obstructed and people's hearts doubted and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power, his judgment was sometimes clouded and men grew wary of him.

sentences.zh: 時負公望者慮為吉甫所忌，多避畏。

translations.literal: At the time those who bore public renown feared Jifu's jealousy and mostly kept away in dread.
translations.idiomatic: Men of public standing feared his jealousy and mostly kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 憲宗潛知其事，未周歲，遂擢用李絳，大與絳不協；

translations.literal: Xianzong secretly knew of this; before a year had passed he promoted Li Jiang, with whom Jifu was greatly at odds;
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong knew this secretly; within the year he elevated Li Jiang, with whom Jifu clashed sharply;

sentences.zh: 而絳性剛評，訐於上前，互有爭論，人多直絳。

translations.literal: while Jiang was by nature blunt in criticism and impeached before the throne; they disputed back and forth and most upheld Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was blunt and spoke against him before the throne; they argued repeatedly, and most sided with Jiang.

sentences.zh: 然性畏慎，雖其不悅者，亦無所傷。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was cautious in fear; even those he disliked he did not harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was cautious by nature and did not harm even those he disliked.

sentences.zh: 服物食味，必極珍美，而不殖財產，京師一宅之外，無他第墅，公論以此重之。

translations.literal: His dress and food were always of the utmost fineness and delicacy, yet he did not amass property; beyond one house in the capital he had no other mansions or villas — public opinion for this held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He dressed and dined lavishly yet amassed no wealth beyond one house in the capital, and public opinion respected him for it.

sentences.zh: 有司謚曰敬憲；

translations.literal: The authorities proposed the posthumous title Jingxian;
translations.idiomatic: The authorities proposed the posthumous name Jingxian;

sentences.zh: 及會議，度支郎中張仲方駁之，以為太優。

translations.literal: at consultation the Treasury director Zhang Zhongfang objected, holding it too generous.
translations.idiomatic: at the review the treasury director Zhang Zhongfang objected that it was too generous.

sentences.zh: 憲宗怒，貶仲方，賜吉甫謚曰忠懿。

translations.literal: Xianzong was angry, demoted Zhongfang, and granted Jifu the posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was angered, demoted Zhongfang, and gave Jifu the posthumous name Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 吉甫嘗討論《易象》異義，附於一行集註之下；

translations.literal: Jifu once discussed variant meanings of the Changes' images, appended beneath Yixing's collected commentary;
translations.idiomatic: Jifu once discussed variant readings of the Changes' images, appended under Yixing's commentary;

sentences.zh: 及綴錄東漢、魏、晉、周、隋故事，訖其成敗損益大端，目為《六代略》，凡三十卷。

translations.literal: and compiled anecdotes of Eastern Han, Wei, Jin, Zhou, and Sui, down to the great points of success, failure, gain, and loss, titled Brief of Six Dynasties, thirty volumes in all.
translations.idiomatic: and compiled tales from Eastern Han through Sui, summarizing success and failure in thirty volumes titled Brief of Six Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 分天下諸鎮，紀其山川險易故事，各寫其圖於篇首，為五十四卷，號為《元和郡國圖》。

translations.literal: He divided the commands of all under Heaven, recorded their mountains, rivers, terrain, hazards, ease, and past affairs, and at the head of each section drew its map — fifty-four volumes, titled Yuanhe Commandery and Principality Maps.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed every command, recorded terrain and history, and placed a map at each section's head in fifty-four volumes titled Yuanhe Commandery and Principality Maps.

sentences.zh: 又與史官等錄當時戶賦兵籍，號為《國計簿》，凡十卷。

translations.literal: He also with the historiographers and others recorded the household levies and military registers of the time, titled Ledger of National Accounting, ten volumes in all.
translations.idiomatic: With the historiographers he recorded current household taxes and military registers in ten volumes titled Ledger of National Accounting.

sentences.zh: 纂《六典》諸職為《百司舉要》一卷。

translations.literal: He compiled the offices of the Six Institutions into Essentials of the Hundred Offices, one volume.
translations.idiomatic: He distilled the offices of the Six Institutions into one volume, Essentials of the Hundred Offices.

sentences.zh: 皆奏上之，行於代。

translations.literal: All were memorialized and submitted, circulating in the age.
translations.idiomatic: All were submitted to the throne and circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子德修、德裕。

translations.literal: His sons were Dexiu and Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Dexiu and Deyu.

sentences.zh: 李籓，字叔翰，趙郡人。

translations.literal: Li Fan, style Shuhan, was a man of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan, styled Shuhan, was from Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖至遠，天後時李昭德薦為天官侍郎，不詣昭德謝恩，時昭德怒，奏黜為壁州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhiyuan, in the time of the Empress Wu, was recommended by Li Zhaode as Vice Director of the Heavenly Ministry; he did not go to Zhaode to thank him for the grace; at the time Zhaode was angry and memorialized to demote him to Prefect of Bibi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhiyuan was recommended by Li Zhaode as vice director of the Heavenly Ministry under the Empress Wu but did not come to thank him; Zhaode had him demoted to prefect of Bibi.

sentences.zh: 祖畬，開元時為考功郎中，事母孝謹，母卒，不勝喪死。

translations.literal: His grandfather She, in the Kaiyuan era was Director of the Bureau of Evaluations, filial and careful in serving his mother; when his mother died he could not bear the mourning and died.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather She was director of evaluations in Kaiyuan, dutiful to his mother; when she died he could not survive the mourning and died.

sentences.zh: 至遠、畬皆以誌行名重一時。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan and She were both famed in their time for moral conduct and resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan and She were both renowned in their day for moral character.

sentences.zh: 父承，為湖南觀察使，亦有名。

translations.literal: His father Cheng was Hunan observation commissioner and likewise had a name.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cheng was commissioner of Hunan and likewise enjoyed repute.

sentences.zh: 籓少恬淡修檢，雅容儀，好學。

translations.literal: In youth Fan was calm and self-restrained in conduct, refined in bearing and appearance, and devoted to learning.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Li Fan was quiet and disciplined, graceful in his bearing, and passionately devoted to study.

sentences.zh: 父卒，家富於財，親族吊者，有挈去不禁，愈務散施，不數年而貧。

translations.literal: When his father died, the family was wealthy in property; among kin who came to mourn, some carried things away without restraint being forbidden; he increasingly devoted himself to scattering gifts, and within a few years was poor.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death the household was rich, yet relatives who came to mourn helped themselves freely and were not stopped; Fan only gave more lavishly away, and within a few years the family was ruined.

sentences.zh: 年四十余未仕，讀書揚州，困於自給，妻子怨尤之，晏如也。

translations.literal: Past forty years of age he had still not taken office; he read books at Yangzhou, distressed at supporting himself; wife and children blamed and resented him, yet he was serene as ever.
translations.idiomatic: Past forty he still held no office, studying at Yangzhou while barely able to feed himself; his wife and children reproached him, yet he remained utterly unperturbed.

sentences.zh: 杜亞居守東都，以故人子署為從事。

translations.literal: Du Ya held office as defender of the Eastern Capital and appointed him as a staff member on account of being an old friend's son.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya was stationed at the Eastern Capital as regional commissioner and took Fan onto his staff as the son of an old friend.

sentences.zh: 洛中盜發，有誣牙將令狐運者，亞信之，拷掠竟罪。

translations.literal: When a robbery broke out in Luoyang, someone falsely accused the ya-general Linghu Yun; Ya believed it, tortured him under interrogation, and finally convicted him.
translations.idiomatic: When a robbery occurred in Luoyang, someone falsely implicated the guard officer Linghu Yun; Du Ya believed the charge, tortured him under interrogation, and finally convicted him.

sentences.zh: 籓知其冤，爭之不從，遂辭出。

translations.literal: Fan knew he was wronged, argued but was not obeyed, and thereupon resigned and left.
translations.idiomatic: Fan knew the man was innocent, pleaded in vain, and resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 後獲真盜宋瞿曇，籓益知名。

translations.literal: Later the real robber Song Qutan was captured, and Fan became still more renowned.
translations.idiomatic: When the real thief, Song Qutan, was later captured, Fan's reputation grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 張建封在徐州，辟為從事，居幕中，謙謙未嘗論細微。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianfeng was at Xuzhou and recruited him as a staff member; he dwelt in the headquarters staff, humble and deferential, never discussing minute matters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianfeng, stationed at Xuzhou, recruited him to his staff; Fan served in the headquarters, modest and reserved, and never meddled in petty affairs.

sentences.zh: 杜兼為濠州刺史，帶使職，建封病革，兼疾驅到府，陰有冀望。

translations.literal: Du Jian was prefect of Haozhou, bearing an envoy's commission; when Jianfeng's illness turned critical, Jian raced to the headquarters, secretly harboring hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jian was prefect of Haozhou with an additional envoy's commission; when Jianfeng fell gravely ill, Jian galloped to headquarters, nursing secret ambitions.

sentences.zh: 籓與同列省建封，出而泣語兼曰：「僕射公奄忽如此，公宜在州防遏，今棄州此來，欲何也？

translations.literal: Fan and colleagues visited the dying Jianfeng; coming out he wept and said to Jian: "The Pushe's lord has suddenly come to this— you ought to be at your prefecture holding things in check; now you have abandoned your prefecture and come here—what do you want?
translations.idiomatic: Fan and his colleagues went to see the dying Jianfeng; as they left, Fan wept and said to Du Jian: "The Minister has fallen so suddenly—you should be at your prefecture keeping order. You have abandoned your post to come here—what do you intend?

sentences.zh: 宜疾去！

translations.literal: You ought to leave quickly!
translations.idiomatic: You must leave at once!

sentences.zh: 不若此，當奏聞。」

translations.literal: If you do not do so, I shall memorialize and report it."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not, I shall report you to the throne."

sentences.zh: 兼錯愕不虞，遂徑歸。

translations.literal: Jian was startled and unprepared, and went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jian was caught off guard and fled straight back to his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建封死，兼悔所誌不就，怨籓甚。

translations.literal: When Jianfeng died, Jian regretted that his aims had not been achieved and deeply resented Fan.
translations.idiomatic: After Jianfeng's death, Du Jian bitterly regretted his thwarted ambitions and hated Fan with a passion.

sentences.zh: 既歸揚州，兼因誣奏籓建封死時搖動軍中。

translations.literal: Once back at Yangzhou, Jian thereupon lodged a false memorial accusing Fan of stirring up the army when Jianfeng died.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Yangzhou, he filed a false report accusing Fan of destabilizing the army at the time of Jianfeng's death.

sentences.zh: 德宗大怒，密詔杜佑殺之。

translations.literal: Dezong was greatly enraged and issued a secret edict to Du You to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong flew into a rage and secretly ordered Du You to execute Fan.

sentences.zh: 佑素重籓，懷詔旬日不忍發，因引籓論釋氏，曰：「因報之事，信有之否？」

translations.literal: You had long valued Fan; he kept the edict for ten days and could not bear to carry it out; he therefore drew Fan into discussing Buddhism and said: "The matter of retribution for causes—is it truly so?"
translations.idiomatic: Du You had always held Fan in high regard; he kept the edict hidden for ten days, unable to act on it, then drew Fan into a discussion of Buddhism, asking: "Do you believe in karmic retribution?"

sentences.zh: 籓曰：「信然。」

translations.literal: Fan said: "It is truly so."
translations.idiomatic: Fan replied: "I do."

sentences.zh: 曰：「審如此，君宜遇事無恐。」

translations.literal: He said: "If it is truly so, you ought to meet affairs without fear."
translations.idiomatic: Du You said: "If that is so, you need not fear whatever comes."

sentences.zh: 因出詔。

translations.literal: He thereupon produced the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Then he produced the secret edict.

sentences.zh: 籓覽之，無動色，曰：「某與兼信為報也。」

translations.literal: Fan read it without change of expression and said: "I and Jian truly have retribution between us."
translations.idiomatic: Fan read it without a flicker of emotion and said: "Du Jian and I were always bound to settle accounts this way."

sentences.zh: 佑曰：「慎勿出口，吾已密論，持百口保君矣。」

translations.literal: You said: "Take care not to let it out of your mouth—I have already argued it in secret and stake a hundred mouths on guaranteeing you."
translations.idiomatic: Du You said: "Say nothing of this—I have already pleaded your case in secret and pledge my family's lives to protect you.

sentences.zh: 德宗得佑解，怒不釋，亟追籓赴闕。

translations.literal: Dezong received You's explanation yet his anger did not subside; he urgently summoned Fan to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong accepted Du You's explanation but would not let his anger go; he urgently summoned Fan to court.

sentences.zh: 及召見，望其儀形，曰：「此豈作惡事人耶！」

translations.literal: When he was summoned for audience and the emperor gazed at his bearing and form, he said: "How could this be a man who does evil deeds!"
translations.idiomatic: When Fan was brought before him, the emperor studied his bearing and exclaimed: "This is no villain!"

sentences.zh: 乃釋然，除秘書郎。

translations.literal: He thereupon was relieved, and Fan was appointed Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His anger lifted, and he appointed Fan Secretary in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 王紹持權，邀籓一相見即用，終不就。

translations.literal: Wang Shao held power and invited Fan, promising that one meeting would bring immediate employment; he ultimately did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao wielded great influence and promised Fan instant appointment if he would only call once; Fan never went.

sentences.zh: 王仲舒、韋成季、呂洞輩為郎官，朋黨輝赫，日會聚歌酒，慕籓名，強致同會，籓不得已一至。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongshu, Wei Chengji, Lü Dong and their sort were court gentlemen; their faction blazed brilliantly; day by day they gathered for song and wine; admiring Fan's name, they forced him to join the same gatherings; Fan, having no choice, went once.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongshu, Wei Chengji, Lü Dong, and their circle were court gentlemen whose clique blazed with influence; they met daily for wine and song, admired Fan's reputation, and dragged him to their parties; he went once, unable to refuse.

sentences.zh: 仲舒輩好為訛語俳戲，後召籓，堅不去，曰：「吾與仲舒輩終日，不曉所與言何也。」

translations.literal: Zhongshu and company delighted in twisted speech and comic play; later when they summoned Fan he firmly would not go and said: "I spend whole days with Zhongshu and company yet do not understand what they are talking about."
translations.idiomatic: They loved obscene jokes and buffoonery; when they summoned Fan again he flatly refused, saying: "I can sit with them all day and still not understand a word they say."

sentences.zh: 後果敗。

translations.literal: Later they indeed met ruin.
translations.idiomatic: They were ruined soon after.

sentences.zh: 遷主客員外郎，尋換右司。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions, and soon exchanged posts to the Right Division.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director in the Bureau of Receptions, then soon transferred to the Right Division of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時順宗冊廣陵王淳為皇太子，兵部尚書王純請改名紹，時議非之，皆云：「皇太子亦人臣也，東宮之臣改之宜也，非其屬而改之，諂也。

translations.literal: At that time Shunzong enfeoffed the Prince of Guangling, Chun, as crown prince; the Minister of War Wang Chun requested to change his name to Shao; contemporary opinion criticized this, all saying: "The crown prince is also a subject among men; it is fitting that the Eastern Palace's ministers change their names— for those not his subordinates to change them is flattery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong invested Prince Chun of Guangling as crown prince, the Minister of War Wang Chun asked to change his name to Shao; opinion turned against him, with many saying: "Even the crown prince is still a subject in name—his own household may change their names, but for outsiders to do so is pure flattery.

sentences.zh: 如純輩豈為以禮事上耶！」

translations.literal: How could men like Chun be said to serve the sovereign with ritual propriety!"
translations.idiomatic: Men like Wang Chun hardly serve their sovereign with proper ritual!"

sentences.zh: 籓謂人曰：「歷代故事，皆自不識大體之臣而失之，因不可復正，無足怪也。」

translations.literal: Fan said to others: "Precedents of successive dynasties were all lost through ministers who did not grasp the larger pattern; because they cannot be set right again, there is nothing to marvel at."
translations.idiomatic: Fan told others: "Every dynasty's precedents were ruined by ministers who could not see the larger picture; once lost they cannot be restored—there is nothing surprising in this."

sentences.zh: 及太子即位，憲宗是也。

translations.literal: When the crown prince ascended the throne—this was Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince took the throne—this was Emperor Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 宰相改郡縣名以避上名，唯監察御史韋淳不改。

translations.literal: The chief ministers changed prefecture and county names to avoid the sovereign's name; only the Investigating Censor Wei Chun did not change.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers changed prefectural and county names to avoid the emperor's personal name; only Investigating Censor Wei Chun refused to change his.

sentences.zh: 既而有詔以陸淳為給事中，改名質；

translations.literal: Soon thereafter there was an edict appointing Lu Chun as Drafting Attendant and changing his name to Zhi;
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict appointed Lu Chun Drafting Attendant and changed his name to Zhi;

sentences.zh: 淳不得已改名貫之，議者嘉之。

translations.literal: Chun had no choice but to change his name to Guanzhi; those who discussed the matter praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chun, left no choice, changed his name to Guanzhi, and public opinion applauded him.

sentences.zh: 籓尋改吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: Fan was soon transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was soon made vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 元和初，遷吏部郎中，掌曹事，為使所蔽，濫用官闕，黜為著作郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, managing bureau affairs; he was obscured by envoys, wantonly used vacant offices, and was demoted to Master of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe reign he became director in the Ministry of Personnel and ran its affairs; swayed by visiting commissioners he abused vacant posts, and was demoted to Master of Writings.

sentences.zh: 轉國子司業，遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Rector of the Directorate of Education, then promoted to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice rector of the Imperial University, then was promoted to Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 制敕有不可，遂於黃敕後批之。
