translations.literal: When an edict or decree was unacceptable, he thereupon annotated it on the back of the yellow edict.
translations.idiomatic: When he found an edict unacceptable, he annotated it directly on the back of the yellow draft.

sentences.zh: 吏曰：「宜別連白紙。」

translations.literal: The clerk said: "You ought to attach separate white paper."
translations.idiomatic: A clerk said: "You should attach a separate sheet of white paper."

sentences.zh: 籓曰：「別以白紙，是文狀，豈曰批敕耶！」

translations.literal: Fan said: "Using separate white paper makes it a document—how could that be called annotating an edict!"
translations.idiomatic: Fan replied: "A separate sheet makes it a routine document—how is that 'annotating the edict'?

sentences.zh: 裴垍言於帝，以為有宰相器，屬鄭絪罷免，遂拜籓門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Pei Ji spoke to the emperor, holding that he had the makings of a chief minister; when Zheng Yin was removed from office, Fan was thereupon appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji told the emperor that Fan had the makings of a chief minister; when Zheng Yin was dismissed, Fan was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent status as Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 籓性忠藎，事無不言，上重之，以為無隱。

translations.literal: Fan's nature was loyal and earnest; on affairs he had nothing he would not speak; the emperor valued him, regarding him as without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was loyal and forthright and spoke his mind on every matter; the emperor prized him as a man who hid nothing.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，顧謂宰臣曰：「前代帝王理天下，或家給人足，或國貧下困，其故何也？」

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year he turned to the chief ministers and said: "Former dynasties' emperors governed All-under-Heaven—some had households provided for and people sufficient, some had the state poor and the lower orders distressed; what were the causes?"
translations.idiomatic: That winter in his fourth year the emperor turned to his chief ministers and asked: "Why did some past emperors bring the realm to plenty while others left the state impoverished and the people in want?"

sentences.zh: 籓對曰：「古人云：『儉以足用。』

translations.literal: Fan replied: "The ancients said: 'Through frugality one attains sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Fan answered: "The ancients said, 'Frugality brings sufficiency.

sentences.zh: 蓋足用系於儉約。

translations.literal: For sufficiency depends on thrift and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Sufficiency rests on thrift and restraint.

sentences.zh: 誠使人君不貴珠玉，唯務耕桑，則人無淫巧，俗自敦本，百姓既足，君孰與不足！

translations.literal: If truly the ruler does not prize pearls and jade but devotes himself solely to plowing and sericulture, then the people will have no excessive craftiness, custom will itself honor the root, the hundred surnames being sufficient— with whom would the ruler not be sufficient!
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign does not prize gems and jade but devotes himself to farming and sericulture, the people shed vain cleverness, custom returns to the fundamentals, and once the common folk are provided for, how could the ruler lack for anything?

sentences.zh: 自然帑藏充羨，稼穡豐登。

translations.literal: Naturally the treasury stores will be full to overflowing and the grain crops abundantly harvested.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury fills of its own accord and the harvests run abundant.

sentences.zh: 若人君竭民力，貴異物，上行下效，風俗日奢，去本務末，衣食益乏，則百姓不足！

translations.literal: If the ruler exhausts the people's strength, prizes strange objects, the higher going and the lower imitating, custom daily growing extravagant, abandoning the root and pursuing the branch, clothing and food increasingly scarce— then the hundred surnames are insufficient!
translations.idiomatic: But if the ruler exhausts the people's strength and prizes exotic luxuries, example flows from above and custom grows ever more extravagant, the root is abandoned for the trivial, and food and clothing run short—then the common people have nothing left!

sentences.zh: 君孰與足！

translations.literal: With whom would the ruler be sufficient!
translations.idiomatic: How then could the ruler himself be provided for?

sentences.zh: 自然國貧家困，盜賊乘隙而作矣！

translations.literal: Naturally the state is poor and households distressed, and bandits seize the gap to arise!
translations.idiomatic: The state grows poor, households fall into distress, and bandits rise to fill the breach!

sentences.zh: 今陛下永鑒前古，思躋富庶，躬尚勤儉，自當理平。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty forever mirrors the past, thinking to ascend to wealth and plenty, personally honoring diligence and frugality— you should naturally attain ordered peace.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty takes the past as your mirror, strives toward abundance, and personally honors diligence and thrift—order and peace should follow of themselves.

sentences.zh: 伏願以知之為非艱，保之為急務，宮室輿馬，衣服器玩，必務損之又損，示人變風，則天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: I humbly wish that you take knowing this as not difficult and preserving it as an urgent task—palaces, carriages and horses, clothing and utensils and playthings—you must strive to reduce them again and again, showing the people a changing wind, and then All-under-Heaven would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to treat knowing this as easy but keeping to it as urgent—palaces, carriages, dress, and ornaments must be pared again and again, so that by your example the realm may change its ways; then the empire would be blessed indeed."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「儉約之事，是我誠心；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The matter of thrift and restraint is my sincere heart;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Frugality is already my sincere intent;

sentences.zh: 貧富之由，如卿所說。

translations.literal: The causes of poverty and wealth are as you have said.
translations.idiomatic: and the causes of wealth and want are just as you describe.

sentences.zh: 唯當上下相勖，以保此道，似有逾濫，極言箴規，此固深期於卿等也。」

translations.literal: Only we ought above and below to encourage one another to preserve this Way; if there seems to be excess and overflow, speak to the utmost in admonition and regulation— this I deeply expect of you all."
translations.idiomatic: We must encourage one another above and below to keep to this path; if anything runs to excess, speak out without reserve—I count deeply on you for that."

sentences.zh: 籓等拜賀而退。

translations.literal: Fan and the others bowed in congratulation and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and his colleagues bowed in thanks and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝又問曰：「禳災祈福之說，其事信否？」

translations.literal: The emperor again asked: "The doctrine of warding off calamity and praying for blessing—is the matter true or not?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again: "Do you believe in rituals to avert disaster and win blessings?"

sentences.zh: 籓對曰：「臣竊觀自古聖達，皆不禱祠。

translations.literal: Fan replied: "Your servant has privately observed that from antiquity the sage and accomplished have all not prayed at shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Fan answered: "In my humble view, the sages of every age never relied on prayer.

sentences.zh: 故楚昭王有疾，卜者謂河為祟，昭王以河不在楚，非所獲罪，孔子以為知天道。

translations.literal: Thus when King Zhao of Chu fell ill, the diviner said the River was the baleful agent; Zhao said the River was not in Chu and was not where guilt was incurred; Confucius held that he knew Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: When King Zhao of Chu fell ill, diviners blamed the River god; Zhao replied that the River lay outside Chu and could not be his to offend—Confucius praised him for understanding Heaven's way.

sentences.zh: 仲尼病，子路請禱，仲尼以為神道助順，系於所行，己既全德，無愧屋漏。

translations.literal: When Zhongni was ill, Zilu requested prayer; Zhongni held that the spirit Way assists the compliant and is tied to what one practices; he himself having perfected virtue, without shame even under the roof-beam.
translations.idiomatic: When Confucius fell ill, Zilu asked to pray for him; Confucius held that the divine way aids the righteous and depends on conduct—having perfected his own virtue, he had nothing to hide even from the spirits under his roof.

sentences.zh: 故答子路云：『丘之禱久矣。』

translations.literal: Thus he answered Zilu: 'I have long been praying.'
translations.idiomatic: He told Zilu: 'I have prayed for a long time already.'

sentences.zh: 《書》云：『惠迪吉，從逆兇。』

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'Following the compliant brings good fortune; following the rebellious brings misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: 'Virtue brings good fortune; rebellion brings ruin.

sentences.zh: 言順道則吉，從逆則兇。

translations.literal: This speaks of following the Way bringing good fortune and following rebellion bringing misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: That is to say, following the Way brings blessing, defying it brings disaster.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：『自求多福。』

translations.literal: The Odes says: 'Seek much blessing for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says: 'Blessings are won by one's own efforts.

sentences.zh: 則禍福之來，鹹應行事，若茍為非道，則何福可求？

translations.literal: Then the coming of misfortune and blessing all responds to conduct; if one recklessly acts against the Way, what blessing can be sought?
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and misfortune alike answer to how one lives; if one persists in wrongdoing, what blessing can prayer obtain?

sentences.zh: 是以漢文帝每有祭祀，使有司敬而不祈，其見超然，可謂盛德。

translations.literal: Thus whenever Emperor Wen of Han had sacrifices, he had the officials be reverent but not pray; his insight was transcendent— it may be called magnificent virtue.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Emperor Wen of Han, whenever sacrifices were held, ordered officials to perform them reverently but not to pray—his vision was sublime, and may truly be called great virtue.

sentences.zh: 若使神明無知，則安能降福；

translations.literal: If the spirits and gods were without knowledge, how could they bestow blessing;
translations.idiomatic: If the spirits were without understanding, how could they grant blessings;

sentences.zh: 必其有知，則私己求媚之事，君子尚不可悅也，況於明神乎！

translations.literal: if they must have knowledge, then private self-seeking and fawning conduct—even a gentleman would not be pleased by it, how much less the bright spirits!
translations.idiomatic: yet if they do understand, private flattery that would shame a gentleman could hardly please the bright spirits!

sentences.zh: 由此言之，則履信思順，自天祐之，茍異於此，實難致福。

translations.literal: Spoken from this, then treading faith and thinking compliance— Heaven itself blesses such; if one differs from this, it is truly hard to bring about blessing.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that those who keep faith and follow the Way are blessed by Heaven; depart from that, and no prayer will win fortune.

sentences.zh: 故堯、舜之德，唯在修己以安百姓。

translations.literal: Thus the virtue of Yao and Shun lay solely in cultivating the self to settle the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: The virtue of Yao and Shun lay solely in perfecting themselves so as to bring peace to the people.

sentences.zh: 管仲云：『義於人者和於神。』

translations.literal: Guan Zhong said: 'Being righteous toward men brings harmony with the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong said: 'He who is just toward men harmonizes with the spirits.

sentences.zh: 蓋以人為神主，故但務安人而已。

translations.literal: For taking men as the spirits' master, one need only devote oneself to settling the people.
translations.idiomatic: Men are the spirits' true concern; the ruler need only devote himself to the people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 虢公求神，以致危亡，王莽妄祈，以速漢兵，古今明誡，書傳所紀。

translations.literal: Duke of Guo sought the spirits and thereby reached peril and ruin; Wang Mang recklessly prayed and thereby hastened the Han armies— clear warnings of past and present, recorded in books and transmissions.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Guo's appeal to the spirits brought ruin upon his state; Wang Mang's frantic prayers only hastened the Han armies—these are plain warnings of past and present, set down in every chronicle.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下每以漢文、孔子之意為準，則百福具臻。」

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty always to take the intentions of Han Wen and Confucius as the standard— then a hundred blessings will all arrive."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to take Emperor Wen and Confucius as your standard in all things, and every blessing will follow."

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 時河東節度使王鍔用錢數千萬賂遺權幸，求兼宰相。

translations.literal: At that time Wang E, military governor of Hedong, used several tens of millions in cash to bribe and gift the powerful and favored, seeking to serve concurrently as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang E, military governor of Hedong, spent tens of millions in bribes to court favorites in hopes of adding the chief ministership to his post.

sentences.zh: 籓與權德輿在中書，有密旨曰：「王鍔可兼宰相，宜即擬來。」

translations.literal: Fan and Quan Deyu were in the Secretariat; there was a secret instruction saying: "Wang E may concurrently serve as chief minister— you ought promptly to draft and submit."
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Quan Deyu were at the Secretariat when a secret order arrived: "Wang E is to be appointed concurrent chief minister—draft the appointment at once."

sentences.zh: 籓遂以筆塗「兼相」字，卻奏上云：「不可。」

translations.literal: Fan thereupon with his brush crossed out the characters "concurrent chief minister," turned the memorial back upward and wrote: "Not permissible."
translations.idiomatic: Fan crossed out the words "concurrent chief minister" with his brush and returned the draft with a single note: "Not acceptable."

sentences.zh: 德輿失色曰：「縱不可，宜別作奏，豈可以筆塗詔耶！」

translations.literal: Deyu turned pale and said: "Even if it is not permissible, you ought to make a separate memorial— how can you use a brush to cross out an edict!"
translations.idiomatic: Quan Deyu blanched and cried: "Even if you refuse, you should draft a separate memorial—how can you deface an imperial order with your pen!"

sentences.zh: 曰：「勢迫矣！

translations.literal: He said: "The pressure is urgent!
translations.idiomatic: Fan said: "There is no time!

sentences.zh: 出今日，便不可止。

translations.literal: Once it leaves today, it cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Once it leaves today, nothing will stop it.

sentences.zh: 日又暮，何暇別作奏！」

translations.literal: The day is again at dusk— what leisure to make a separate memorial!"
translations.idiomatic: Dusk is already here—who has time for another memorial!"

sentences.zh: 事果寢。

translations.literal: The matter indeed was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫自揚州再入相，數日，罷籓為詹事。

translations.literal: Li Jifu from Yangzhou entered the chief ministership again; within days Fan was removed and made Crown Prince's Household Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu returned from Yangzhou to the chief ministership; within days Fan was dismissed to serve as administrator of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 後數月，上思籓，召對，復有所論列。

translations.literal: Several months later the emperor thought of Fan, summoned him for audience, and again he set forth arguments in array.
translations.idiomatic: Months later the emperor missed Fan, summoned him for audience, and again heard his forthright counsel.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，出為華州刺史、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he went out as prefect of Huazhou and concurrent Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he was sent out as prefect of Hua Prefecture with concurrent status as Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 未行卒，年五十八，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Before he set out on the journey he died, aged fifty-eight; he was posthumously given the Ministry of Revenue minister.
translations.idiomatic: He died before he could take up the post, at fifty-eight; the court posthumously appointed him Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 籓為相材能不及裴垍，孤峻頗後韋貫之，然人物清規，亦其流也。

translations.literal: Fan as chief minister: in talent he did not reach Pei Ji; in solitary sternness he was somewhat behind Wei Guanzhi— yet in personal character and pure standards he was also of their stream.
translations.idiomatic: As a chief minister Fan lacked Pei Ji's ability and fell somewhat short of Wei Guanzhi's austere integrity, yet in character and moral clarity he belonged to the same company.

sentences.zh: 權德輿，字載之，天水略陽人。

translations.literal: Quan Deyu, style name Zaizhi, was a man of Lüeyang in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Deyu, whose style was Zaizhi, came from Lüeyang in Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 父臯，字士繇，後秦尚書翼之後。

translations.literal: His father Gao, style name Shiyao, was a descendant of Yi, Minister of the Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan Gao, style Shiyao, was descended from Yi, a minister of the Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 少以進士補貝州臨清尉。

translations.literal: In youth, having passed the jinshi examination, he was appointed to fill the post of Linqing district magistrate in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, after passing the jinshi examination, he was appointed magistrate of Linqing district in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 安祿山以幽州長史充河北按察使，假其才名，表為薊縣尉，署從事。

translations.literal: An Lushan, as Youzhou chief secretary filling the Hebei surveillance commissioner, borrowed his talent and reputation, memorialized him as Jixian district magistrate, and appointed him as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan, serving as chief secretary of Youzhou and Hebei surveillance commissioner, coveted his reputation, recommended him as magistrate of Ji district, and took him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 臯陰察祿山有異志，畏其猜虐，不可以潔退，欲潛去，又慮禍及老母。

translations.literal: Gao secretly observed that Lushan harbored a different intent; he feared his suspicious cruelty and could not withdraw with clean propriety; he wished to slip away secretly, yet also worried that disaster would reach his aged mother.
translations.idiomatic: Gao secretly perceived that Lushan harbored rebellious ambitions; fearing his suspicious cruelty, he could not resign openly, wished to flee in secret, yet dreaded that his aged mother would suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 天寶十四年，祿山使臯獻戎俘，自京師回，過福昌。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao, Lushan had Gao present barbarian captives; returning from the capital he passed through Fuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao, Lushan sent Gao to present captives at court; on his return from the capital he passed through Fuchang.

sentences.zh: 福昌尉仲謨，臯從父妹婿也，密以計約之。

translations.literal: Zhong Mo, district magistrate of Fuchang, was Gao's cousin's daughter's husband; he secretly made a plan and pledged with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Mo, magistrate of Fuchang, was married to Gao's cousin's daughter; the two secretly agreed on a plan.

sentences.zh: 比至河陽，詐以疾亟召謨，謨至，臯示已喑，瞪謨而瞑。

translations.literal: When they reached Heyang, he feigned acute illness and urgently summoned Mo; when Mo arrived, Gao showed that he was already mute, stared at Mo and closed his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Near Heyang he feigned a grave illness and urgently summoned Zhong Mo; when Mo arrived, Gao showed that he had lost his voice, stared at him, and closed his eyes as if dead.

sentences.zh: 謨乃勉哀而哭，手自含襲，既逸臯而葬其棺，人無知者。

translations.literal: Mo thereupon forced grief and wept, with his own hands placed the mouth-pearl and shroud; having let Gao escape, he buried the coffin— no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: Mo forced himself to wail in mourning, placed the burial ornaments with his own hands, then helped Gao escape and buried the coffin in his place—no one was the wiser.

sentences.zh: 從吏以詔書還，臯母初不知，聞臯之死，慟哭傷行路。

translations.literal: The attendant returned with the edict; Gao's mother at first did not know; hearing of Gao's death, she wailed so bitterly that passersby on the road were stricken.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant returned with the imperial message; Gao's mother knew nothing at first, but when she heard her son was dead she wailed so bitterly that everyone on the road was moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 祿山不疑其詐死，許其母歸。

translations.literal: Lushan did not suspect the feigned death and permitted his mother to return.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan never suspected the ruse and allowed his mother to go home.

sentences.zh: 臯時微服匿跡，候母於淇門；

translations.literal: Gao at the time wore plain clothes and hid his tracks, waiting for his mother at Qimen;
translations.idiomatic: Gao went in disguise and hid his trail, waiting for his mother at Qimen;

sentences.zh: 既得侍其母，乃奉母晝夜南去，及渡江，祿山已反矣。

translations.literal: Once he was able to attend his mother, he then escorted her south day and night; by the time they crossed the river, Lushan had already rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Once he could be with his mother again, he took her south without rest day or night; by the time they crossed the Yangzi, Lushan had already risen in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 由是名聞天下。

translations.literal: From this his fame spread throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment his name was known everywhere under heaven.

sentences.zh: 淮南采訪使高適表臯試大理評事，充判官。

translations.literal: Huainan surveillance commissioner Gao Shi memorialized recommending Gao for trial appointment as Libationer-evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, to serve as judge-assessor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shi, surveillance commissioner of Huainan, recommended Gao for a probationary post as evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review and appointed him judge-assessor on his staff.

sentences.zh: 屬永王璘亂，多劫士大夫以自從，臯懼見迫，又變名易服以免。

translations.literal: When the Yong Prince Li Lin rebelled, many scholar-officials were seized to follow him; Gao feared being compelled and again changed his name and attire to escape.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebellion of the Yong Prince Li Lin, who seized many scholar-officials to follow him, Gao feared being forced into service and again changed his name and dress to slip away.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在蜀，聞而嘉之，除監察御史。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong in Shu, hearing of it, commended him and appointed him investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong, then in Shu, heard the story and praised him, appointing him investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 會丁母喪，因家洪州。

translations.literal: He happened to enter mourning for his mother and therefore made his home in Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he entered mourning and settled his household in Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時南北隔絕，或逾歲不聞詔命。

translations.literal: At the time north and south were cut off from each other; sometimes more than a year would pass without hearing an imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: North and south were then cut off from one another, and sometimes more than a year would pass without word of an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 有中使奉宣至洪州，經時未復，過有求取，州縣苦之。

translations.literal: A palace envoy arrived in Hongzhou bearing an imperial message; after a long time he did not return, yet often made demands—the prefecture and counties found it burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: A palace envoy came to Hongzhou on imperial business; he lingered for a long time without leaving and kept making demands, to the great distress of the prefecture and counties.

sentences.zh: 時有王遘為南昌令，將執按之，因見臯白其事；

translations.literal: At the time Wang You was magistrate of Nanchang and was about to arrest and prosecute him; he therefore went to see Gao and explained the matter;
translations.idiomatic: Wang You was then magistrate of Nanchang and was about to arrest the envoy; he went to Gao and told him what he intended;

sentences.zh: 臯不言，久之，垂涕曰：「方今何由可致一敕使，而遽有此言。」

translations.literal: Gao did not speak; after a long while, with tears falling he said: "In the present age how could one possibly summon even one imperial messenger, and yet you so hastily speak such words."
translations.idiomatic: Gao said nothing. After a long silence tears fell as he said, "In times like these, how could we ever hope to see even one imperial messenger again—and you speak so rashly of this?"

sentences.zh: 因掩涕而起，遘遽拜謝之。

translations.literal: He thereupon wiped his tears and rose; You hurriedly bowed and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: He wiped his tears and stood; You at once bowed and apologized.

sentences.zh: 浙西節度使顏真卿表臯為行軍司馬，詔征為起居舍人，又以疾辭。

translations.literal: Zhexi military commissioner Yan Zhenqing memorialized appointing Gao as campaigning marshal; an edict summoned him as Attendant of the Left, but again he declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing, military commissioner of Zhexi, recommended Gao as campaigning marshal; an edict summoned him as attendant of the left, but again he declined, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「本自全吾誌，豈受此之名耶！」

translations.literal: He once said: "I originally wished only to preserve my own purpose—how could I accept such a title!"
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "I only wanted to keep faith with my own purpose—why should I take such an office!"

sentences.zh: 李季卿為江淮黜陟使，奏臯節行，改著作郎，復不起。

translations.literal: Li Jiqing, as Jianghuai promotion-and-demotion commissioner, memorialized Gao's integrity and conduct; he was reassigned as Composition Academician, but again did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiqing, promotion-and-demotion commissioner for the Jianghuai region, memorialized Gao's integrity; he was made composition academician but again refused to take office.

sentences.zh: 兩京蹂於胡騎，士君子多以家渡江東，知名之士如李華、柳識兄弟者，皆仰臯之德而友善之。

translations.literal: The two capitals were trampled by barbarian horsemen; many scholar-gentlemen crossed with their families east of the River; renowned men such as Li Hua and the brothers Liu Shi all looked up to Gao's virtue and befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: When the two capitals were overrun by rebel horsemen, many gentlemen crossed east of the Yangzi with their households; famous men such as Li Hua and the brothers Liu Shi all admired Gao's character and became his friends.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年，卒於家，年四十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali, he died at home, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Dali reign he died at home, aged forty-six.

sentences.zh: 元和中謚曰貞孝。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe reign he was posthumously titled Pure and Filial.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era he was given the posthumous title Pure and Filial.

sentences.zh: 初，臯卒，韓洄、王定為服朋友之喪，李華為其墓表，以為分天下善惡，一人而已。

translations.literal: At first, when Gao died, Han Hui and Wang Ding observed mourning as for a friend's funeral; Li Hua composed his tomb inscription, deeming that to divide good and evil in the realm required only one man.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao died, Han Hui and Wang Ding mourned him as they would a close friend; Li Hua wrote his tomb inscription, declaring that to weigh good and evil in the world one needed only this single man.

sentences.zh: 前贈秘書監，至是因子德輿為相，立家廟。

translations.literal: Previously he had been posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat; at this time, because his son Deyu became chief minister, a family ancestral temple was established.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier been posthumously made director of the Secretariat; now, because his son Deyu became chief minister, a family ancestral temple was established.

sentences.zh: 至元和十二年，復贈太子太保。

translations.literal: By the twelfth year of Yuanhe, he was again posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe he was again posthumously made grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 德輿生四歲，能屬詩；

translations.literal: Deyu at age four could compose poetry;
translations.idiomatic: Deyu at four could compose verse;

sentences.zh: 七歲居父喪，以孝聞；

translations.literal: at seven, while observing mourning for his father, he became known for filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: at seven, while mourning his father, he was already famed for filial devotion;

sentences.zh: 十五為文數百篇，編為《童蒙集》十卷，名聲日大。

translations.literal: at fifteen he wrote several hundred literary pieces, compiled as the Collected Beginner's Writings in ten scrolls, and his reputation grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: at fifteen he had written several hundred pieces, gathered into ten scrolls titled Collected Writings of Youth, and his fame grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 韓洄黜陟河南，辟為從事，試秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Han Hui, as Henan promotion commissioner, recruited him as a staff member; he was tried as collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Hui served as promotion commissioner for Henan he recruited Deyu to his staff and had him tried as collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，復為江西觀察使李兼判官，再遷監察御史。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenyuan he again served as judge-assessor to Jiangxi observation commissioner Li Jian, and was promoted again to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan he again served as judge-assessor under Li Jian, observation commissioner of Jiangxi, and was soon promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 府罷，杜佑、裴胄皆奏請，二表同日至京。

translations.literal: When the prefecture staff was dissolved, both Du You and Pei Zhou memorialized requesting him; the two memorials arrived at the capital on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: When that office was dissolved, both Du You and Pei Zhou memorialized asking for him, and the two petitions reached the capital on the same day.

sentences.zh: 德宗雅聞其名，徵為太常博士，轉左補闕。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong had long heard his name and summoned him as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then transferred him to Left Supplementation Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong had long known his reputation and summoned him as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then transferred him to left supplementation attendant.

sentences.zh: 八年，關東大水，上疏請降詔恤隱，遂命奚陟等四人使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, a great flood struck east of the Pass; he submitted a memorial requesting an edict to relieve distress; the emperor thereupon dispatched Xi Zhi and three others as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year a great flood struck east of the Pass; he memorialized asking that an edict be issued to relieve suffering, and the emperor sent Xi Zhi and three others as envoys.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡以巧幸判度支，九年，自司農少卿除戶部侍郎，仍判度支。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling, through clever favoritism, was assigned to oversee the Treasury; in the ninth year he was promoted from Vice Minister of Agriculture to Vice Minister of Revenue, still overseeing the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling, through artful favor, was put in charge of the treasury; in the ninth year he was promoted from vice minister of agriculture to vice minister of revenue while still overseeing the treasury.

sentences.zh: 德輿上疏曰：

translations.literal: Deyu submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Deyu submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣伏以爵人於朝，與眾共之，況經費之司，安危所系。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly considers that ennobling a man at court is a matter to be shared with the multitude; how much more the office of state revenues, on which security and peril depend.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject humbly reflects that to advance a man at court is a matter for all to judge together—and how much more the office that controls the state's funds, on which the realm's safety depends.

sentences.zh: 延齡頃自權判，逮今間歲，不稱之聲，日甚於初。

translations.literal: Yanling not long ago took temporary charge; up to now nearly a year has passed, and voices of disapproval grow daily stronger than at first.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling has held acting charge of the office for nearly a year now, and complaints against him grow louder with each passing day.

sentences.zh: 群情眾口，喧於朝市，不敢悉煩聖聽，今謹略舉所聞。

translations.literal: The sentiment of the multitude clamors in the court and marketplace; I dare not weary Your Majesty's ears with it all—I now respectfully cite in brief what I have heard.
translations.idiomatic: Public outrage fills the court and the markets; I dare not weary Your Majesty with every detail and will only summarize what I have heard.

sentences.zh: 多雲以常賦正額支用未盡者，便為剩利，以為己功。

translations.literal: Many say that whenever funds from the regular tax quota remained unspent, he treated the surplus as profit and claimed it as his own merit.
translations.idiomatic: Many say that whenever regular tax revenues were not fully spent, he treated the remainder as surplus profit and claimed the credit for himself.

sentences.zh: 又重破官錢買常平先所收市雜物，遂以再給估價，用充別貯利錢。

translations.literal: Again he broke the treasury to buy miscellaneous goods previously purchased by the Ever-Normal Granaries, then reissued them at appraised value to fill separate stored profit funds.
translations.idiomatic: Again he spent public funds to buy back miscellaneous goods the Ever-Normal Granaries had already purchased, then reissued them at appraised prices to pad separate profit accounts.

sentences.zh: 又雲邊上諸軍皆至懸闕，自今春已來，並不支糧。

translations.literal: Again they say that frontier armies have all reached desperate shortage; since this spring none has been issued grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: They also say that frontier armies are utterly destitute and that since this spring no rations have been issued at all.

sentences.zh: 伏以疆場之事，所虞非細，誠聖謨前定，終事切有司。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly considers that frontier matters are no trifling concern; truly the sage plan is foreordained, yet execution rests with the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject humbly notes that frontier affairs are no small matter; though Your Majesty's strategy is settled in advance, carrying it out still depends on the responsible officials.

sentences.zh: 陛下必以延齡孤貞獨立，為時所抑，醜正有黨，結此流言，何不以新收剩利，征其本末，為分析條奏？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty deems Yanling upright and isolated, slandered by the times, with a faction of ugly uprights weaving these rumors—why not take the newly collected surplus profits, trace their origin and end, and present an itemized analysis?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty believes Yanling stands alone in integrity and has been slandered by a clique of the corrupt, why not trace the newly reported surpluses from beginning to end and submit an itemized account?

sentences.zh: 又擇朝賢信臣，與中使一人巡覆邊軍，察其資儲有無虛實。

translations.literal: Again select a worthy minister of the court and one palace envoy to tour and review the frontier armies, inspecting whether their supplies are real or empty.
translations.idiomatic: Send a trusted minister of the court together with a palace envoy to tour the frontier armies and verify whether their stores are real or merely on paper.

sentences.zh: 倘延齡受任已來，精心勤力，每事省約，別收羨余，於正數各有區分，邊軍儲蓄，實猶可支，身自斂怨，為國惜費；

translations.literal: If since Yanling took office he has been diligent and devoted, sparing in all affairs, separately gathering surplus within the regular accounts, with frontier stores truly adequate, bearing resentment himself to save the state's expense;
translations.idiomatic: If, since taking office, Yanling has worked with scrupulous care, economized in every matter, kept surpluses separate from regular accounts, and left the frontier armies genuinely supplied while bearing resentment himself to save the state money;

sentences.zh: 自宜更示優獎，以洗群疑，明書厥勞，昭示天下。

translations.literal: then he should receive still greater favor and reward to wash away the crowd's doubts, with his merit clearly recorded and proclaimed to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: then he should receive still greater honors to clear away suspicion, with his achievements written plainly and proclaimed to the realm.

sentences.zh: 如或言者非謬，罔上實多，豈以邦國重務，委之非據！

translations.literal: If the speakers are not wrong and deception of superiors is indeed great—how could the weighty affairs of the state be entrusted to one unfit for the post!
translations.idiomatic: But if the reports are true and he has deceived his superiors on a grand scale, how can the weightiest affairs of state be left in unworthy hands!

sentences.zh: 臣職在諫曹，合采群議，正拜已來，今已旬日，道路云云，無不言此。

translations.literal: Your subject's office is in the remonstrance bureau; I ought to gather public opinion—since his formal appointment, now ten days have passed, and on the roads everywhere none fails to speak of this.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject serves in the remonstrance bureau and ought to gather public opinion; since Yanling's formal appointment ten days ago, travelers everywhere speak of nothing else.

sentences.zh: 豈京師士庶之眾，愚智之多，合而為黨，共有仇嫉。

translations.literal: Could the multitudes of scholars and commoners in the capital, the many wise and foolish together, have formed a faction sharing one grudge?
translations.idiomatic: Could all the learned and common people of the capital, wise and foolish alike, have banded together in one faction out of shared spite?

sentences.zh: 陛下亦宜稍回聖鑒，俯察群心。

translations.literal: Your Majesty also ought slightly to turn the sage mirror and look down to discern the hearts of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should also turn the mirror of your judgment and look down to see what the people truly feel.

sentences.zh: 況臣之事君，如子事父；

translations.literal: Moreover, the subject's service to his ruler is like a son's to his father;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a subject serves his ruler as a son serves his father;

sentences.zh: 今當聖明不諱之代，若猶愛身隱情，是不忠不孝，莫大之罪。

translations.literal: now in an age of sage brilliance where nothing is taboo, if one still cherishes the body and hides the truth, that is disloyalty and unfilial conduct—the greatest of crimes.
translations.idiomatic: in an age as enlightened as this, when nothing is taboo, to cherish one's safety and hide the truth is the greatest disloyalty and unfiliality.

sentences.zh: 敢瀝肝血，伏待刑書。

translations.literal: I dare pour out my heart's blood and humbly await the penal writ.
translations.idiomatic: I pour out my heart's blood and humbly await whatever punishment Your Majesty may decree.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Attendant of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made attendant of the left.

sentences.zh: 歲中，兼知制誥。

translations.literal: Within the year he additionally took charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Later that year he was also put in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 轉駕部員外郎、司勛郎中，職如舊。

translations.literal: Transferred to Vice Director in the Transport Bureau and Director in the Bureau of Merit Records, his duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director in the Transport Bureau and director in the Bureau of Merit Records, while keeping his former duties.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Promoted to Secretariat Draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretariat draftsman.

sentences.zh: 是時，德宗親覽庶政，重難除授，凡命於朝，多補自禦劄。

translations.literal: At this time Dezong personally reviewed all government affairs and greatly hesitated over appointments; whatever was ordered at court was largely filled in from his own brush annotations.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Dezong personally oversaw every branch of government and weighed appointments with great care; most court offices were filled from his own brush notes.

sentences.zh: 始，德輿知制誥，給事有徐岱，舍人有高郢；

translations.literal: At first, when Deyu was in charge of edicts, the reviewing officer was Xu Dai and the draftsman was Gao Ying;
translations.idiomatic: When Deyu first took charge of edicts, Xu Dai served as reviewing officer and Gao Ying as draftsman;

sentences.zh: 居數歲，岱卒，郢知禮部貢舉，獨德輿直禁垣，數旬始歸。

translations.literal: After several years Dai died; Ying took charge of the Ministry of Rites examination; Deyu alone stood duty in the inner precincts and only after many tens of days returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After several years Dai died; Ying took charge of the civil examinations, and Deyu alone kept watch in the inner palace, sometimes going many weeks before he could return home.

sentences.zh: 嘗上疏請除兩省宮，德宗曰：「非不知卿之勞苦，禁掖清切，須得如卿者，所以久難其人。」

translations.literal: He once memorialized requesting that inner-palace posts be filled; Dezong said: "It is not that I do not know your hardships—the inner precincts are solemn and exacting and require someone like you; that is why for so long it has been hard to find the right person."
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized asking that additional staff be appointed in the two secretariats. Dezong replied, "It is not that I do not know your hardships. The inner palace demands precision and needs someone like you—that is why I have found no one to replace you for so long."

sentences.zh: 德輿居西掖八年，其間獨掌者數歲。

translations.literal: Deyu dwelt in the western secretariat eight years, during which he alone held charge for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu served in the western secretariat for eight years, several of them with no colleague at all.

sentences.zh: 貞元十七年冬，以本官知禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan he served in his existing office overseeing the Ministry of Rites examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan he was put in charge of the civil examinations while retaining his existing post.

sentences.zh: 來年，真拜侍郎，凡三歲掌貢士，至今號為得人。

translations.literal: The following year he was formally appointed Vice Minister; for three years altogether he directed the examinations, and to this day he is said to have chosen worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was formally made vice minister; for three years he directed the examinations, and to this day he is remembered for choosing worthy men.

sentences.zh: 轉戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 元和初，歷兵部、吏部侍郎，坐郎吏誤用官闕，改太子賓客，復為兵部侍郎，遷太常卿。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanhe he served in succession as Vice Minister of War and of Personnel; because a clerk wrongly used an office vacancy he was demoted to Mentor of the Heir Apparent, again made Vice Minister of War, and promoted to Director of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he served in turn as vice minister of war and of personnel; when a clerk misused an office title he was demoted to mentor of the heir apparent, then restored as vice minister of war and promoted to director of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，宰相裴垍寢疾，德輿拜禮部尚書、平章事，與李籓同作相。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year, chief minister Pei Ji lay ill; Deyu was appointed Minister of Rites and Grand Councilor, serving as chief minister together with Li Fan.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year chief minister Pei Ji fell gravely ill; Deyu was made minister of rites and grand councilor, serving as chief minister alongside Li Fan.

sentences.zh: 河中節度王鍔來朝，貴幸多譽鍔者，上將加平章事，李籓堅執以為不可。

translations.literal: Hedong military commissioner Wang E came to court; many favorites praised him; the emperor was about to add him as Grand Councilor; Li Fan firmly held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E, military commissioner of Hedong, came to court; many favorites praised him, and the emperor was about to make him grand councilor, but Li Fan firmly objected.

sentences.zh: 德輿繼奏曰：「夫平章事，非序進而得，國朝方鎮帶宰相者，蓋有大忠大勛。

translations.literal: Deyu followed with a memorial saying: "The office of Grand Councilor is not gained by orderly advancement; in our dynasty military commissioners who bore the chief minister title generally had great loyalty and great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu followed with a memorial: "The office of grand councilor is not won by orderly promotion. In our dynasty, when a regional commander bore the title of chief minister, it was because he had shown great loyalty and great merit.

sentences.zh: 大歷已來，又有跋扈難制者，不得已而與之。

translations.literal: Since Dali there have also been arrogant and hard-to-control ones, given the title only because there was no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Dali era there have also been arrogant men too powerful to control, and the title was granted only because there was no choice.

sentences.zh: 今王鍔無大忠勛，又非姑息之時，欲假此名，實恐不可！」

translations.literal: Now Wang E has no great loyalty or merit, and this is no longer a time of indulgent appeasement—to lend him this title truly cannot be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang E has shown no such loyalty or merit, and this is no longer an age of appeasement. To lend him that title would be a grave mistake!"

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 運糧使董溪、于臯謨盜用官錢，詔流嶺南。

translations.literal: Grain-transport commissioners Dong Xi and Yu Gaomo misappropriated government funds; an edict exiled them to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xi and Yu Gaomo, grain-transport commissioners, embezzled public funds; an edict banished them to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 行至湖外，密令中使皆殺之。

translations.literal: When they reached beyond the lakes, a secret order directed palace envoys to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the lake districts, a secret order sent palace envoys to kill them all.

sentences.zh: 他日，德輿上疏曰：

translations.literal: On another day Deyu submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion Deyu submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 竊以董溪等，當陛下憂山東用兵時，領糧料供軍重務，聖心委付，不比尋常；

translations.literal: Your subject ventures that Dong Xi and the others, during Your Majesty's anxiety over campaigning in Shandong, bore the weighty charge of leading grain supplies to the army—the sage heart entrusted them, not as with ordinary cases;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject ventures that Dong Xi and his colleagues, at a time when Your Majesty was deeply concerned over the war in Shandong, held the grave responsibility of supplying the armies with grain—charges entrusted by the imperial heart, not ordinary offices;

sentences.zh: 敢負恩私，恣其贓犯，使之萬死，不足塞責。

translations.literal: they dared betray favor for private gain and indulged their corrupt offenses; even ten thousand deaths would not suffice to answer for it.
translations.idiomatic: they betrayed that trust for private gain and gave free rein to corruption; even death ten thousand times over would not answer for their guilt.

sentences.zh: 弘寬大之典，流竄太輕，陛下合改正罪名，兼責臣等疏略。

translations.literal: To apply the great magnanimous standard, exile and banishment are too light; Your Majesty ought to correct the charges and also blame your ministers for our oversight.
translations.idiomatic: To apply the great law of magnanimity, exile is too light; Your Majesty should revise the charges and also hold your ministers accountable for our oversight.

sentences.zh: 但詔令已下，四方聞知，不書明刑，有此處分，竊觀眾情，有所未喻。

translations.literal: Yet the edict has already been issued and the four quarters have heard; without setting forth clear punishment, yet with this disposition—your subject observes the public sentiment and finds something not understood.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the edict has already gone forth and the realm has heard of it; punishment was not set forth clearly, yet this disposition was made—your subject observes the public mood and finds much that people do not understand.

sentences.zh: 伏自陛下臨禦已來，每事以誠，實與天地合德，與四時同符，萬方之人，沐浴皇澤。

translations.literal: Humbly, since Your Majesty ascended the throne, in every matter you have acted with sincerity, truly in virtue with Heaven and Earth, in accord with the four seasons, and the people of the ten thousand regions bathe in imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly, since Your Majesty ascended the throne you have acted with sincerity in every matter, truly sharing the virtue of Heaven and Earth and moving in harmony with the seasons, and the people of the realm have bathed in imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 至如於、董所犯，合正典章，明下詔書，與眾同棄，即人各懼法，人各謹身。

translations.literal: As for the offenses of Yu and Dong, they ought to be rectified by the proper statutes; let an edict be clearly issued and they be cast off together with the multitude—then each man will fear the law and each will guard himself.
translations.idiomatic: As for the crimes of Yu and Dong, they should be judged by the proper statutes; let an edict be issued plainly and they be cast out before all—then every man will fear the law and guard his conduct.

sentences.zh: 臣誠知其罪不容誅，又是已過之事，不合論辯，上煩聖聰。

translations.literal: Your subject truly knows their crime admits no excuse for sparing, and this is moreover a matter already past, unfit for debate and burdening the sage ear.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject knows full well that their crimes deserve no mercy, and that this matter is already past and unfit to debate, burdening Your Majesty's ear.

sentences.zh: 伏以陛下聖德聖姿，度越前古，頃所下一詔，舉一事，皆合理本，皆順人心。

translations.literal: Humbly, Your Majesty's sage virtue and sage bearing surpass all previous ages; every edict recently issued, every matter undertaken, has accorded with reason's root and followed the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly, Your Majesty's sage virtue and bearing surpass all previous ages; every edict you have lately issued, every act you have undertaken, has accorded with principle and followed the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 伏慮他時更有此比，但要有司窮鞫，審定罪名，或致之極法，或使自盡，罰一勸百，孰不甘心！

translations.literal: Humbly I fear that hereafter there may again be such cases; only let the responsible offices exhaust investigation, fix the charges, either bring them to the utmost penalty or have them take their own lives—punishing one to admonish a hundred; who would not willingly submit!
translations.idiomatic: I fear that similar cases may arise hereafter; let the responsible offices investigate thoroughly, fix the charges, and either bring the guilty to the utmost penalty or have them take their own lives—punish one to warn a hundred, and who would not submit willingly!

sentences.zh: 巍巍聖朝，事體非細，臣每於延英奏對，退思陛下求理之言，生逢盛明，感涕自賀。

translations.literal: In this august sage court the matter is no trifle; your subject whenever he responds at court in the Yanying Hall, on retiring ponders Your Majesty's words seeking good governance—born into such brilliance, I am moved to tears and congratulate myself.
translations.idiomatic: In this august sage court the matter is no small one; whenever I answer at court in the Yanying Hall and retire, I ponder Your Majesty's words on seeking good governance—born into such an age of brilliance, I am moved to tears and count myself fortunate.

sentences.zh: 況以愚滯樸訥，聖鑒所知，伏惟恕臣迂疏，察臣丹懇。

translations.literal: Moreover, as one slow-witted, blunt, and plain-spoken—known to the sage scrutiny—I humbly beg forgiveness for my roundabout ignorance and ask you to perceive my red heart's earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as one slow-witted, blunt, and plain-spoken—as Your Majesty well knows—I humbly beg you to forgive my roundabout manner and perceive the earnestness of my heart.

sentences.zh: 及李吉甫自淮南詔徵，未一年，上又繼用李絳。

translations.literal: When Li Jifu was summoned by edict from Huainan, within less than a year the emperor again successively employed Li Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jifu was summoned by edict from Huainan, within less than a year the emperor also brought in Li Jiang.

sentences.zh: 時上求理方切，軍國無大小，一付中書。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was urgently seeking good governance; military and civil affairs large and small were all entrusted to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was urgently seeking good governance, and military and civil affairs great and small were all entrusted to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 吉甫、絳議政頗有異同，或於上前論事，形於言色；

translations.literal: Jifu and Jiang differed considerably in governing discussion; sometimes before the emperor they debated affairs, showing it in word and countenance;
translations.idiomatic: Jifu and Jiang often differed in council, sometimes debating before the throne until their disagreement showed plainly in word and face;

sentences.zh: 其有詣於理者，德輿亦不能為發明，時人以此譏之。

translations.literal: when there were points that accorded with reason, Deyu also could not clarify them—contemporaries for this ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: when a point was sound, Deyu could not clarify it either, and contemporaries ridiculed him for it.

sentences.zh: 竟以循默而罷，復守本官。

translations.literal: In the end he was dismissed for following silence and meek compliance, returning to his original office.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was dismissed for following along in silence and returned to his former office.

sentences.zh: 尋以檢校吏部尚書為東都留守，後拜太常卿，改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Acting Minister of Personnel and Eastern Capital guardian; later appointed Director of Imperial Sacrifices, then changed to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting minister of personnel and guardian of the eastern capital; later he was appointed director of imperial sacrifices and then minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 先是，許孟容、蔣乂等奉詔刪定格敕。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xu Mengrong, Jiang Yi, and others received an edict to revise and fix the codified ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xu Mengrong, Jiang Yi, and others had received an edict to revise the codified ordinances.

sentences.zh: 孟容等尋改他官，乂獨成三十卷，表獻之，留中不出。

translations.literal: Mengrong and others soon transferred to other offices; Yi alone completed thirty scrolls, memorialized and presented them, but they were kept within the palace and not released.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong and the others soon moved to other posts; Yi alone completed thirty scrolls, memorialized and presented them, but the emperor kept them in the palace and did not release them.

sentences.zh: 德輿請下刑部，與侍郎劉伯芻等考定，復為三十卷奏上。

translations.literal: Deyu requested they be sent down to the Ministry of Justice to be examined and fixed with Vice Minister Liu Bozhu and others; again thirty scrolls were submitted upward.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu asked that the work be sent to the Ministry of Justice for review with Vice Minister Liu Bozhu and others; thirty scrolls were revised and submitted again.

sentences.zh: 十一年，復以檢校吏部尚書出鎮興元。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he again went out as acting Minister of Personnel to command Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he again went out as acting minister of personnel to take command at Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 十三年八月，有疾，詔許歸闕，道卒，年六十。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year he fell ill; an edict permitted him to return to court; he died on the road, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year he fell ill; an edict allowed him to return to court, but he died on the road, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈左僕射，謚曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; posthumous title Literary.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and given the posthumous title Literary.

sentences.zh: 德輿自貞元至元和三十年間，羽儀朝行，性直亮寬恕，動作語言，一無外飾，蘊藉風流，為時稱向。

translations.literal: From Zhenyuan through thirty years of Yuanhe Deyu was an ornament of the court processions; his nature was upright, bright, and forgiving; in movement and speech he had no outward adornment, yet kept inward elegance and grace, and his contemporaries praised and looked to him.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years from Zhenyuan through Yuanhe Deyu was an ornament of the court; upright, candid, and forgiving by nature, he showed no outward affectation in bearing or speech, yet carried inward grace and refinement, and his age looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 於述作特盛，《六經》百氏，遊泳漸漬，其文雅正而弘博，王侯將相洎當時名人薨歿，以銘紀為請者什八九，時人以為宗匠焉。

translations.literal: In literary composition he was especially prolific; the Six Classics and the hundred schools he swam in and steeped himself; his writing was refined, correct, and vast; of kings, marquises, generals, ministers, and famous men of the time who died, eight or nine in ten asked him for epitaphs and records—the age regarded him as a master craftsman.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially prolific as a writer, steeped in the Six Classics and the hundred schools; his prose was refined, correct, and vast. Eight or nine out of ten kings, marquises, generals, ministers, and famous men of the day who died asked him to write their epitaphs and records, and the age regarded him as a master craftsman.

sentences.zh: 尤嗜讀書，無寸景暫倦，有文集五十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: He especially loved reading—not even a moment's span did he rest from weariness—and had a collected works of fifty scrolls circulating in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He especially loved reading and never rested even for a moment; his collected works ran to fifty scrolls and circulated widely in his time.

sentences.zh: 子璩，中書舍人。

translations.literal: His son Quan Ji was a Secretariat draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quan Ji served as secretariat draftsman.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：裴垍精鑒默識，舉賢任能，啟沃帝心，弼諧王道。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Pei Ji had keen discernment and silent knowledge, raised the worthy and employed the able, nourished the emperor's mind, and harmonized the kingly Way.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Pei Ji combined sharp judgment with quiet insight, promoted talent and put ability to use, nourished the emperor's mind, and aligned the realm with the kingly Way.

sentences.zh: 如崔群、裴度、韋貫之輩，鹹登將相，皆垍之薦達。

translations.literal: Men such as Cui Qun, Pei Du, and Wei Guanzhi all rose to generals and chancellors through Ji's recommendation and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Cui Qun, Pei Du, and Wei Guanzhi all reached the highest civil and military offices through Ji's patronage.

sentences.zh: 立言立事，知無不為。

translations.literal: In establishing words and establishing affairs, wherever he knew, he did not fail to act.
translations.idiomatic: In counsel and in action alike, he left nothing undone that he knew should be done.

sentences.zh: 吉甫該洽典經，詳練故實，仗裴垍之抽擢，致朝倫之式序。

translations.literal: Jifu was comprehensive in the classics and statutes and thorough in precedents; relying on Pei Ji's lifting up of talent, he brought court ethics into proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu mastered the classics and precedents; with Pei Ji's help in elevating talent, he set court conduct in proper order.

sentences.zh: 吉甫知垍之能別髦彥，垍知吉甫之善任賢良，相須而成，不忌不克。

translations.literal: Jifu knew Ji's ability to distinguish outstanding men; Ji knew Jifu's skill in employing the worthy; they needed each other to succeed, without jealousy or obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu knew Ji could spot outstanding men; Ji knew Jifu could employ the worthy. They complemented each other without jealousy or rivalry.

sentences.zh: 叔翰修身慎行，力學承家，批制敕有夕郎之風，塗御書見宰執之器；

translations.literal: Shuhan cultivated the person and was cautious in conduct, studied hard and inherited the family tradition; in drafting edicts he had the manner of an evening secretary, and in brushwork for imperial writings one saw the capacity of a chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: Shuhan cultivated himself with care, studied hard in the family tradition, drafted edicts with the polish of a Secretariat drafter, and wrote imperial calligraphy with the bearing of a chief minister;

sentences.zh: 而乃輕財散施，天爵是期，偉哉，自待之意也！

translations.literal: yet he lightly regarded wealth and gave it away in charity, setting his hope on Heaven's nobility—how grand was the way he held himself!
translations.idiomatic: yet he treated wealth lightly and gave freely, aiming at honor from Heaven—how lofty was his self-regard!

sentences.zh: 德輿孝悌力學，髫齔有聞，疏延齡恣行巧佞，論臯謨不書明刑，三十年羽儀朝行，實臯之余慶所鐘。

translations.literal: Deyu was filial and fraternal, studied hard, and was famed from childhood; he memorialized against Yan Shouling's unrestrained craft and flattery, and in discussing Gao Yao's counsel did not record clear punishments; for thirty years he was an ornament of the court procession—truly the lingering blessing bestowed on Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was filial, studious, and famed from boyhood; he denounced Yan Shouling's flattery, argued in discussing Gao Yao's counsel without recording capital punishment, and for thirty years adorned the court—a true heir to his father's legacy.

sentences.zh: 此四子者，所謂經緯之臣，又何慚於王佐矣！

translations.literal: These four men are what are called ministers who weave the warp and woof of state—how should they blush before kingly assistants!
translations.idiomatic: These four were true architects of the state—what shame need they feel before the greatest of royal counselors!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：二李秉鈞，信為名臣。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: The two Lis held the scales of state—truly they were famed ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy reads: The two Lis held the helm of state—worthy name indeed among ministers.

sentences.zh: 甫柔而黨，籓俊而純。

translations.literal: Jifu was supple yet partisan; Fan was eminent yet pure.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu was supple yet given to faction; Fan was brilliant yet upright.

sentences.zh: 裴公鑒裁，朝無屈人。

translations.literal: Lord Pei's discernment and judgment—at court no worthy man was left unraised.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Pei's eye for talent left no worthy man unrewarded at court.

sentences.zh: 權之藻思，文質彬彬。

translations.literal: Quan's literary thought—ornament and substance in graceful balance.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's literary grace balanced refinement and substance in equal measure.
